metadata.title: Universal Canonical Race and Stat Block Registry
metadata.canonical_priority: The campaign system package overrides obsolete wording in individual source documents.
metadata.drilthar_correction: Marsh absorbs Swamp; six bloodlines total; all breathe underwater.
metadata.jaspey_correction: Mosscap, Gloomtail, and Rotcap are non-bloodline forms/caste expressions.

canon_authority.authority_rule: The canonical 22-god order and dedicated creator compendium govern every deity-to-people relationship; province and settlement placement does not alter divine parentage or race canon.

categories.family_description: Humans, Near-Humans, and Mixed Heritage contains the canonical parent races Human, Half-Elf (choose an Elven-Type), Half-Orc (Human + Orc ancestry), Khoravar Half-Elf (choose an Elven-Type), and Umbral Human. Human retains its five established lineage options. Half-Elf and Khoravar Half-Elf each choose one of 21 Elven-Type ancestries: the 15 Elf bloodlines or one of the six Kaluseban bloodlines. All of these ancestries remain under Nebyrr's single creator category.
categories.creation_doctrine: Canonical race-compendium doctrine: Nebyrr holds this single creator category through civilization, lineage, dynasties, marriage, inheritance, and social order. The canonical parent races are Human, Half-Elf (choose an Elven-Type), Half-Orc (Human + Orc ancestry), Khoravar Half-Elf (choose an Elven-Type), and Umbral Human. Human retains its five established lineage options. Half-Elf and Khoravar Half-Elf each choose one of 21 Elven-Type ancestries: the 15 Elf bloodlines or one of the six Kaluseban bloodlines. Temple language preserves reverence, but its colder margins classify each race, bloodline, lineage, and form by yield, pressure, environment, devotion, fear, beauty, endurance, and the particular note it awakens in the god's appetite.
categories.created_peoples_record: Nebyrr is recorded as the single creator-god of the Humans, Near-Humans, and Mixed Heritage category: Human, Half-Elf (choose an Elven-Type), Half-Orc (Human + Orc ancestry), Khoravar Half-Elf (choose an Elven-Type), and Umbral Human. Human retains its five established lineage options. Half-Elf and Khoravar Half-Elf each choose one of 21 Elven-Type ancestries: the 15 Elf bloodlines or one of the six Kaluseban bloodlines. The public hymn calls this lineage and blessing; the older register reads like curated divine husbandry, sorting bodies, habitats, temperaments, and spirit-resonance so civilization, lineage, dynasties, marriage, inheritance, and social order never depends on one mortal pattern alone.

parent_races.name: Human
parent_races.description: Humans are highly adaptable and found in nearly every environment across the world. They are known for their cultural diversity, short generational cycles, and unmatched versatility among mortal races. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.

canonical_subtypes.name: Standard Human
canonical_subtypes.description: Humans are highly adaptable and found in nearly every environment across the world. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

canonical_subtypes.name: Umbral Human
canonical_subtypes.description: Umbral humans are touched by shadowed ancestry or planar darkness, giving them an eerie presence. They often possess heightened perception in low light and a natural affinity for secrecy or introspection. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

canonical_subtypes.name: Half-Elf
canonical_subtypes.description: Half-elves are dual-natured beings born of human and elven lineage, often balancing ambition with longevity. They tend to struggle with identity but excel at diplomacy, adaptability, and bridging cultures. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

canonical_subtypes.name: Khoravar

canonical_subtypes.name: Half-Orc

parent_races.name: Genasi
parent_races.description: Genasi are elemental humanoids whose mortal bodies express a clear elemental ancestry. In Universal, Genasi are one parent race with Air, Earth, Fire, and Water lineages rather than four unrelated top-level races. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.

canonical_subtypes.name: Air Genasi
canonical_subtypes.description: Born of living wind and storm currents, Air Genasi bodies often feel lighter than they should be and are naturally attuned to altitude and motion. They are frequently seen as distant or restless, as if always partially elsewhere in the sky. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

canonical_subtypes.name: Earth Genasi
canonical_subtypes.description: Forged from stone, metal, or deep earth pressure, Earth Genasi possess dense, enduring bodies that resist harm and hardship. They are typically steady and patient, valuing permanence and reliability above change. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

canonical_subtypes.name: Fire Genasi
canonical_subtypes.description: Touched by living flame, Fire Genasi often carry warmth in their presence and sometimes literal embers within their form. They are intense and driven, prone to passion that can either inspire or destroy. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

canonical_subtypes.name: Water Genasi
canonical_subtypes.description: Shaped by tide and current, Water Genasi bodies flow with subtle adaptability and can endure pressure others cannot. They are emotionally fluid and deeply responsive to surrounding energies and environments. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

parent_races.name: Elemental Kin
parent_races.description: Elemental Kin are humanoid peoples whose bodies lean toward a living elemental state without being Genasi or Panolima. In standard selection, Flamekin and Rimekin are bloodlines under this parent race. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.

canonical_subtypes.name: Flamekin
canonical_subtypes.description: Small, volatile beings of concentrated fire essence, Flamekin flicker with unstable inner heat that reflects their emotions. They are quick to act and quick to burn out if not tempered. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

canonical_subtypes.name: Rimekin
canonical_subtypes.description: Born of frost and glacial energy, Rimekin carry cold within their bones and often leave traces of ice in their wake. They are calm and detached, valuing control and restraint. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

parent_races.name: Elementborn
parent_races.description: Elementborn are people shaped by a dominant environmental or elemental birth-state. In Universal, Ashborn, Azureborn, Bogborn, Deepborn, Snowborn, and Stoneborn are lineages of one Elementborn parent race. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.

canonical_subtypes.name: Ashborn
canonical_subtypes.description: Created from volcanic ash and elemental aftermath, Ashborn embody both destruction and rebirth. They are survivors who adapt quickly to devastation and change. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

canonical_subtypes.name: Azureborn
canonical_subtypes.description: Infused with stormlight and arcane sky-energy, Azureborn shimmer with faint electric or luminous traits. They are curious and analytical, often drawn to patterns in chaos. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

canonical_subtypes.name: Bogborn
canonical_subtypes.description: Shaped by stagnant wetlands and decaying elemental mire, Bogborn thrive in toxicity and slow, heavy environments. They are patient, secretive, and highly resilient in adverse conditions. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

canonical_subtypes.name: Deepborn
canonical_subtypes.description: Born from abyssal pressure and deep elemental convergence, Deepborn are adapted to crushing depths and silence. They are introspective and often perceive reality in slow, layered ways. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

canonical_subtypes.name: Snowborn
canonical_subtypes.description: Manifested from persistent winter cycles and frozen wind, Snowborn carry the stillness of long cold seasons. They are disciplined and emotionally restrained, but deeply enduring. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

canonical_subtypes.name: Stoneborn
canonical_subtypes.description: Hardened from living rock and continental force, Stoneborn bodies are near-immovable and highly durable. They are grounded thinkers who prefer stability and long-term planning. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

parent_races.name: Panolima
parent_races.description: Living Embodiments of Elemental Harmony: Earth, Fire, Water, Air, and Aether. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.

canonical_subtypes.name: Earth Bloodline
canonical_subtypes.description: You gain a climbing speed of 20 feet on stone, trees, cliffs, or earthen surfaces. You have advantage on checks made to detect unstable ground, structural weaknesses, mineral deposits, or hidden natural passages. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

canonical_subtypes.name: Fire Bloodline
canonical_subtypes.description: You gain resistance to fire damage. You can shed bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for an additional 10 feet. Once per long rest, when you deal fire damage, you may add your proficiency bonus to one damage roll. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

canonical_subtypes.name: Water Bloodline
canonical_subtypes.description: You gain a swimming speed equal to your walking speed and can breathe air and water. You ignore movement penalties from nonmagical currents, mud, ice, or shallow water. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

canonical_subtypes.name: Air Bloodline
canonical_subtypes.description: Your walking speed increases by 5 feet. When you jump or fall, you may glide up to 20 feet horizontally and reduce falling damage by five times your level. You have advantage on checks involving wind, storms, pressure changes, or airborne sounds. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

canonical_subtypes.name: Aether Bloodline
canonical_subtypes.description: You gain resistance to force damage from environmental magical surges or arcane storms. At 3rd level, you may cast detect magic once per long rest. At 5th level, you may cast misty step once per long rest, appearing as a pulse of elemental light. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.

parent_races.name: Triton
parent_races.description: Oceanic guardians adapted to deep-sea environments and coastal defense, Triton are disciplined and duty-bound. They often serve as protectors of aquatic realms. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.

parent_races.name: Locathah
parent_races.description: Aquatic survivors shaped by hardship and scarcity, Locathah are resilient and cautious. They value freedom from oppression and stable waters. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.

parent_races.name: Grung
parent_races.description: Small amphibious frogfolk with toxic physiology and strict caste systems, Grung are communal and hierarchical. They are highly territorial and survival-focused. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.

parent_races.name: Merfolk
parent_races.description: Half-fish humanoids of oceanic civilizations, Merfolk are culturally rich and deeply social. They thrive in community-based underwater societies. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.

parent_races.name: Sahuagin
parent_races.description: Predatory sea-dwellers adapted for brutality and conquest, Sahuagin are aggressive and hierarchical. They value strength and dominance in all forms. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.

parent_races.name: Lotol
parent_races.description: Mysterious amphibious marshfolk with adaptive camouflage and bioluminescent traits, Lotol are elusive and observant. They prefer secrecy and environmental harmony. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.

parent_races.name: Nakudama
parent_races.description: Deepwater mystics attuned to currents and oceanic magic, Nakudama perceive tides as living consciousness. They are spiritual and highly intuitive navigators. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.

parent_races.name: Dril'thar
parent_races.description: Amphibious Mystics of the Living Waters. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.

canonical_subtypes.name: Grassland Bloodline
canonical_subtypes.description: Grassland Dril'thars evolved among flooded plains, seasonal rivers, colossal reed-seas, and wind-swept wetlands where speed and stealth ensured survival. Their coloration often resembles pale reeds, dusty greens, muddy browns, and storm-gray camouflage. Grassland Dril'thars excel as scouts, skirmishers, survivalists, and mobile martial combatants. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy. Every Dril'thar bloodline can breathe underwater.

canonical_subtypes.name: Lush Forest Bloodline
canonical_subtypes.description: Forest Dril'thars evolved within misty temperate forests, root-choked wetlands, and rain-soaked valleys. Their coloration trends toward bark-browns, moss-greens, fungal whites, and muted amber patterns. Forest Dril'thars excel at infiltration, mobility, and wilderness survival. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy. Every Dril'thar bloodline can breathe underwater.

canonical_subtypes.name: Marsh Bloodline
canonical_subtypes.description: Marsh Dril'thars are the single canonical wetland bloodline, encompassing marsh, swamp, bog, fen, and mixed-wetland adaptations. Their coloration and traits vary with local wetland ecology. Every Dril'thar bloodline has external gills and can breathe underwater. Temple marginalia records this as a canonical ancestry structure within the deity's single creator category.

canonical_subtypes.name: Rainforest Bloodline
canonical_subtypes.description: Rainforest Dril'thars inhabit colossal jungle canopies, flooded jungles, mangrove labyrinths, and sacred spawning forests. Their bodies blaze with sapphire blues, sunset oranges, orchid purples, vibrant greens, and glowing bioluminescent markings. Rainforest Dril'thars are among the greatest primal mystics and jungle survivalists of their people. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy. Every Dril'thar bloodline can breathe underwater.

canonical_subtypes.name: Ocean Bloodline
canonical_subtypes.description: Ocean Dril'thars evolved among abyssal trenches, open seas, storm coasts, and deep-ocean migratory clans. They can breathe underwater due to their ear appendages evolving a gill-like filtering system. Their bodies are sleek and streamlined, patterned in silver-gray gradients, abyssal black, deep blues, and glowing. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

canonical_subtypes.name: Reef Bloodline
canonical_subtypes.description: Reef Dril'thars dwell among coral kingdoms, volcanic shallows, mangrove reefs, and bioluminescent underwater cities. Their skin patterns resemble tropical fish coloration, coral blooms, and glowing reef organisms. Reef Dril'thars often become navigators, diplomats, illusionists, and mystics. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy. Every Dril'thar bloodline can breathe underwater.

Temple marginalia records this as a canonical ancestry structure within the deity's single creator category.

Every Dril'thar bloodline can breathe underwater.

Their bodies are sleek and streamlined, patterned in silver-gray gradients, abyssal black, deep blues, and glowing. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

canonical_register.name: Dril'thar Bloodline - Reef Bloodline

base_traits.name: Overview
base_traits.description: Your Dril’thar character has the following racial traits.

base_traits.name: Ability Score Increase
base_traits.description: Increase one ability score by 2 and another ability score by 1, or increase three different ability scores by 1 each.

base_traits.name: Creature Type
base_traits.description: You are a Humanoid.

base_traits.name: Age
base_traits.description: Dril’thars hatch from gelatinous egg-clutches and rapidly mature during their early metamorphic stages. Most reach adulthood around age 10. Typical Dril’thars live between 50 and 70 years, though certain deep-water or mystical bloodlines may survive for centuries.

base_traits.name: Size
base_traits.description: Dril’thars vary dramatically between lineages and environmental adaptations. Your size is either Small or Medium (choose when selecting this race).

base_traits.name: Speed
base_traits.description: Your base walking speed is 30 feet. You also have: A swimming speed equal to your walking speed A climbing speed equal to your walking speed

base_traits.name: Amphibious
base_traits.description: You can breathe both air and water.

subtypes.name: Grassland Bloodline
subtypes.canonical_description: Grassland Dril'thars evolved among flooded plains, seasonal rivers, colossal reed-seas, and wind-swept wetlands where speed and stealth ensured survival. Their coloration often resembles pale reeds, dusty greens, muddy browns, and storm-gray camouflage. Grassland Dril'thars excel as scouts, skirmishers, survivalists, and mobile martial combatants. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy. Every Dril'thar bloodline can breathe underwater.

Dril’thar Physiology
Dril’thars are highly polymorphic amphibious humanoids whose bodies constantly adapt through lineage, mutation, environment, and magical evolution. No two Dril’thar communities develop exactly alike.

A Dril’thar bloodline may resemble sleek poison dart frogs with radiant warning colors, while another develops translucent jellyfish-like skin, gecko-like climbing pads, bioluminescent markings, elongated grasping tongues, venomous mucus secretions, or abyssal deep-sea adaptations.
Despite their diversity, all Dril’thars share several defining biological traits:
Constantly moist skin coated in toxic mucus
Large unblinking eyes that must be periodically moistened with the tongue
Feathery axolotl-like sensory organs along the sides of the head that detect vibrations through water, wood, mud, and stone
Fully prehensile tails used for balance, climbing, and manipulation
Long muscular tongues capable of grasping objects or anchoring the body
Adhesive climbing pads allowing movement across walls and ceilings
Extreme dependence on moisture and humidity

Their coloration varies enormously depending on lineage and habitat: murky swamp-greens, coral pinks, luminous blues, fungal grays, mossy browns, abyssal blacks, vibrant rainforest oranges, and glowing bioluminescent patterns are all common among different clans.
Dril’thar Traits
Your Dril’thar character has the following racial traits.
Ability Score Increase
Increase one ability score by 2 and another ability score by 1, or increase three different ability scores by 1 each.
Creature Type
You are a Humanoid.
Age
Dril’thars hatch from gelatinous egg-clutches and rapidly mature during their early metamorphic stages. Most reach adulthood around age 10.
Typical Dril’thars live between 50 and 70 years, though certain deep-water or mystical bloodlines may survive for centuries.
Size
Dril’thars vary dramatically between lineages and environmental adaptations.
Your size is either Small or Medium (choose when selecting this race).
Speed
Your base walking speed is 30 feet.
You also have:
A swimming speed equal to your walking speed
A climbing speed equal to your walking speed
Amphibious
You can breathe both air and water.
Core Dril’thar Traits
Leapbound Movement
Your powerful amphibian legs allow explosive bursts of movement.
Your long jump and high jump distances are tripled, and you do not require a running start to jump.
Adhesive Climber
Your adhesive hands, feet, tail, and abdomen allow you to scale nearly any surface.

You can climb difficult surfaces, including upside-down across ceilings, without needing to make an ability check, provided your hands and feet are free and you are not wearing equipment that prevents adhesion.
Prehensile Tail
You possess a muscular prehensile tail capable of stabilizing your body and manipulating objects.
Your tail can:
Hold or carry small objects
Retrieve stowed items
Open simple containers
Assist with climbing or balance
Your tail cannot wield weapons or shields.
You also have advantage on ability checks or saving throws made to maintain balance or resist being shoved prone.
Prehensile Tongue
Your elongated muscular tongue can extend up to 15 feet.
As a bonus action, you may use your tongue to:
Retrieve a Tiny unattended object weighing no more than 10 pounds
Manipulate a simple mechanism
Pull yourself 5 feet toward a surface
Attempt to grapple a Medium or smaller creature
Tongue grapples use Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics).
Your tongue cannot make weapon attacks unless granted by another feature.
Hypervibrational Hearing
The feathery axolotl-like organs along the sides of your head detect subtle vibrations through water and solid surfaces.
You gain:
Proficiency in the Perception skill
Advantage on Perception checks involving hearing or vibrations
Blindsight out to 10 feet while touching water, mud, wood, stone, or another solid surface
Toxic Mucus
Your skin secretes poisonous defensive mucus.
When a creature grapples you or hits you with an unarmed strike, it takes poison damage equal to your proficiency bonus.
You also gain:
Resistance to poison damage
Advantage on saving throws against the poisoned condition
Eyeless Rest
Dril’thars cannot blink.

To keep your eyes moist, you instinctively lick them with your tongue during periods of rest or inactivity. Because of your constant sensory awareness, you have advantage on saving throws against being surprised while conscious.
Moisture Dependency
Your biology depends upon constant hydration and humidity.
If you go longer than 8 hours without significant humidity, rainfall, immersion, mud, or water exposure, you gain one level of exhaustion.
This exhaustion cannot be removed until you spend at least 1 hour submerged, soaked, or resting within a saturated environment.
Amphibious Resilience
You have advantage on saving throws against diseases caused by spoiled water, fungal infection, swamp rot, natural contaminants, or similar environmental hazards.
Dril’thar Mysticism
The spiritual traditions of the Dril’thars intertwine healing, illusion, weather-reading, water magic, and ancestral communion.
Mystic Healing
You gain proficiency in the Medicine skill.
You may cast cure wounds once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to do so after finishing a long rest.
Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for this spell.
Amphibious Mysticism
You know the minor illusion cantrip.
At 3rd level, you may cast detect magic once without expending a spell slot.
At 5th level, you may cast misty step once without expending a spell slot.
You regain the ability to cast these spells after finishing a long rest.
Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

All Dril’thars descend from ancient amphibious bloodlines shaped by their environments. Choose one lineage.

Ancient Dril’thar civilizations often organized themselves into biological caste systems tied to coloration, mutation, and spawning lineage.
Some surviving dynasties still maintain hereditary roles:
Green — hunters, scouts, laborers, warriors
Blue — artisans, navigators, reef-builders
Purple — tacticians, commanders, administrators
Red — healers, scholars, mystics
Orange — elite warriors and royal guardians
Gold — sovereigns, priest-kings, ancient bloodlines
Modern Dril’thars increasingly reject rigid hierarchy. Adaptability, survival, spiritual power, and wisdom matter more than birth.
A Marsh necromancer may become a healer. A Rainforest mystic may lead warriors. A Grassland hunter may ascend to rulership through conquest, endurance, or prophecy.
To the Dril’thars, identity is fluid like water itself.

The Dril’thars are an ancient amphibious people whose civilizations rise from swamps, flooded jungles, coral reefs, mangrove coasts, subterranean rivers, mist-choked marshes, and sacred rainforests. Across countless regions of the world, they are known as healers, navigators, mystics, hunters, survivalists, and wandering pilgrims capable of thriving where most civilizations would collapse.

To outsiders, Dril’thars are often misunderstood as poisonous frogfolk, territorial swamp-creatures, or eerie marsh spirits. In truth, they are one of the most biologically adaptable and spiritually complex peoples in existence.

Their philosophy teaches that all things move in cycles: rain becomes river, river becomes sea, decay becomes renewal, and death feeds life anew. Water is not merely an element to the Dril’thar—it is memory, ancestry, spirit, and destiny itself. A spawning pool may serve simultaneously as temple, cemetery, and place of prophecy, for the Dril’thars believe the currents of the world carry the echoes of those who came before.

Though ancient Dril’thar empires once enforced rigid biological caste systems based on coloration, mutation, and spawning lineage, many modern clans reject such traditions entirely. Some become wandering reef-clans, nomadic marsh tribes, jungle mystic circles, or independent explorer societies. Adventuring Dril’thars are often exiles, scholars, mercenaries, healers, mystics, treasure-seekers, or pilgrims searching for meaning beyond the waters that birthed them.

sections.heading: Core Dril’thar Traits
content: Your powerful amphibian legs allow explosive bursts of movement.
Your long jump and high jump distances are tripled, and you do not require a running start to jump.
Your adhesive hands, feet, tail, and abdomen allow you to scale nearly any surface.

You can climb difficult surfaces, including upside-down across ceilings, without needing to make an ability check, provided your hands and feet are free and you are not wearing equipment that prevents adhesion.
You possess a muscular prehensile tail capable of stabilizing your body and manipulating objects.
Your tail can:
Hold or carry small objects
Retrieve stowed items
Open simple containers
Assist with climbing or balance
Your tail cannot wield weapons or shields.
You also have advantage on ability checks or saving throws made to maintain balance or resist being shoved prone.
Your elongated muscular tongue can extend up to 15 feet.
As a bonus action, you may use your tongue to:
Retrieve a Tiny unattended object weighing no more than 10 pounds
Manipulate a simple mechanism
Pull yourself 5 feet toward a surface
Attempt to grapple a Medium or smaller creature
Tongue grapples use Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics).
Your tongue cannot make weapon attacks unless granted by another feature.
The feathery axolotl-like organs along the sides of your head detect subtle vibrations through water and solid surfaces.
You gain:
Proficiency in the Perception skill
Advantage on Perception checks involving hearing or vibrations
Blindsight out to 10 feet while touching water, mud, wood, stone, or another solid surface
Your skin secretes poisonous defensive mucus.
When a creature grapples you or hits you with an unarmed strike, it takes poison damage equal to your proficiency bonus.
You also gain:
Resistance to poison damage
Advantage on saving throws against the poisoned condition
Dril’thars cannot blink.

To keep your eyes moist, you instinctively lick them with your tongue during periods of rest or inactivity. Because of your constant sensory awareness, you have advantage on saving throws against being surprised while conscious.
Your biology depends upon constant hydration and humidity.
If you go longer than 8 hours without significant humidity, rainfall, immersion, mud, or water exposure, you gain one level of exhaustion.
This exhaustion cannot be removed until you spend at least 1 hour submerged, soaked, or resting within a saturated environment.
You have advantage on saving throws against diseases caused by spoiled water, fungal infection, swamp rot, natural contaminants, or similar environmental hazards.

sections.heading: Dril’thar Society
content: Ancient Dril’thar civilizations often organized themselves into biological caste systems tied to coloration, mutation, and spawning lineage.
Some surviving dynasties still maintain hereditary roles:
Green — hunters, scouts, laborers, warriors
Blue — artisans, navigators, reef-builders
Purple — tacticians, commanders, administrators
Red — healers, scholars, mystics
Orange — elite warriors and royal guardians
Gold — sovereigns, priest-kings, ancient bloodlines
Modern Dril’thars increasingly reject rigid hierarchy. Adaptability, survival, spiritual power, and wisdom matter more than birth.
A Marsh necromancer may become a healer. A Rainforest mystic may lead warriors. A Grassland hunter may ascend to rulership through conquest, endurance, or prophecy.
To the Dril’thars, identity is fluid like water itself.

sections.heading: Universal Alignment Profile
content: Typical race profile: Neutral Guardian — The quiet heart of the group: protective, compassionate, communal, and kind without needing rigid institutions.

Dril'thars are aquatic mystics, healers, hunters, navigators, and pilgrims shaped by living water and renewal. Modern Dril'thar clans can reject old caste rigidity while keeping communal care and spiritual integrity.

MOL use: Use Dril'thars as marsh sages, reef healers, river guides, living-water priests, or clan protectors. Older imperial bloodlines can lean more lawful or more selfish depending on how much caste legacy remains.

sections.heading: Marsh Bloodline (Canonical Wetland Bloodline)
content: Marsh Dril'thars are the single canonical wetland bloodline, encompassing marsh, swamp, bog, fen, and mixed-wetland adaptations. Their coloration and traits vary with local wetland ecology. Every Dril'thar bloodline has external gills and can breathe underwater. Temple marginalia records this as a canonical ancestry structure within the deity's single creator category.

Overview. Swamp Dril’thars are ancient survivors adapted to toxic bogs, fungal wetlands, stagnant marshes, and blackwater rivers. Their skin is often black-green, mold-speckled gray, algae blue, or dark olive.
Bog Venom. When a creature fails a saving throw against your Toxic Mucus, its speed is reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn.
Mire Camouflage. While in heavy rain, mud, marshland, dense vegetation, or swamp water, you may attempt to Hide even when lightly obscured.
Drowning Grasp. Creatures grappled by your tongue or tail have disadvantage on checks made to escape.

Overview. Marsh Dril’thars dwell among drowned ruins, corpse-marshes, fungal floodplains, grave bogs, and mist-choked wetlands where decay feeds renewal. Their coloration resembles corpse-gray algae, pallid moss, black reeds, muted violet rot-patterns, and sickly pale blues.

Gravewater Affinity. You know the chill touch cantrip. At 3rd level, you may cast false life once per long rest. At 5th level, you may cast gentle repose once per long rest. Constitution, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells (choose when selecting this lineage).
Necrotic Symbiosis. You gain resistance to necrotic damage.
Carrion Sense. You automatically know the location of corpses, undead, or dying creatures within 30 feet if they are touching the same body of water, mud, or ground as you.

races.name: Tamhiogal
races.summary: Aquatic Bettafolk of Hydromancy, Coral Stewardship, and Tidal Spirits. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.
player_lore: Tamhiogals are aquatic beings. They resemble betta fish in their coloration, displaying vibrant shades of blues, purples, teals, and crimsons that shift with emotion and magical activity. On land, they possess scaled, graceful humanoid arms and legs, with scales rippling along their cheeks, necks, and collarbones. Their eyes are liquid and reflective, glowing faintly in dim light, and their hair consists of bioluminescent, jellyfish-like strands that can sting mildly when threatened.

In water, they have gills along their necks, webbing between fingers and elbows, and fins along the spine, knees, and tail. Their legs are replaced by long, sleek caudal fins, with dorsal and anal fins enhancing maneuverability. Tamhiogals require hydration and tidal energy, which regenerate most efficiently in aquatic environments. They sustain themselves through fish, kelp, and other sea-based foods.

Being immersed in water naturally maintains their hygiene and overall well-being. Exposure to polluted or stagnant water causes spiritual and emotional dissonance, while ritual bathing and communion with ocean spirits restore clarity, mood, and magical flow. Tamhiogals possess abilities attuned to both water and land. They can transition smoothly between terrestrial and aquatic forms, allowing fluid movement across both environments.

They can communicate with marine creatures and spirits, summon temporary aquatic allies, and manipulate water through hydromancy, creating healing surges, protective barriers, or offensive tidal waves. Water responds instinctively to their presence, enhancing both their mobility and magical efficacy. Tamhiogals are guardians and stewards of water, shaping coral formations, guiding currents, and ensuring the sanctity of oceans, rivers, and other aquatic environments. Their connection to water influences their emotions, abilities, and interactions, making them both mystical and deeply attuned to the tides of Universal.

player_lore: The Geisamahis are small, agile creatures . They resemble large ferrets or stoats but walk upright and possess opposable thumbs, allowing them to manipulate objects with precision. Their bodies are wiry and compact, built for speed, nimbleness, and the ability to navigate tight spaces, while their elongated snouts, expressive eyes, and twitching whiskers reflect their alertness and curiosity. Fur varies in earthy browns, fiery oranges, and snowy whites, often with individualized patterns, and many adorn themselves with small tools, belts, and pouches containing gadgets or relics.

They are highly adaptable, thriving in forests, ruins, urban alleys, or other cluttered or complex environments, and they maintain mental sharpness through exploration, invention, and playful problem-solving. Geisamahis have heightened senses and dexterity, allowing them to detect hidden passages, traps, or valuable items that others might miss. They are quick learners and excel at crafting devices, tools, and improvised mechanisms to aid in survival or exploration. Their movements are fluid and acrobatic, capable of extended jumps, climbing, and rapid dashes, enabling them to evade danger or reach otherwise inaccessible areas.

They possess a natural instinct for teamwork, often coordinating with kin or allies in subtle, synchronized ways. Their energy and vitality are maintained through frequent rest, light, energy-rich meals, and exposure to natural environments. Geisamahis exhibit keen awareness of their surroundings, sensing traps, subtle hazards, or changes in terrain that might threaten their safety. Their small stature and nimble frame allow them to slip unnoticed through gaps or under cover, and their reflexes enable rapid reactions to threats.

They communicate through gestures, expressions, and subtle vocalizations, and their presence often conveys curiosity, mischief, or intelligence. Their culture emphasizes adaptability, invention, and self-reliance, and they often live in tight-knit groups that share knowledge and resources. Geisamahis are persistent problem-solvers, thriving in situations that demand cleverness or unconventional approaches. Their physical and mental traits are closely tied to their magical sustenance, making arcane energy and enchanted environments particularly vital to their well-being.

They are resourceful, inventive, and always seeking ways to outthink challenges or obstacles in their path. Geisamahis appear as upright, fur-covered creatures with large, expressive eyes and long whiskers that twitch in response to their surroundings. Their nimble hands and opposable thumbs allow them to handle tools, gadgets, or delicate objects with precision. They move quickly and lightly, capable of scaling obstacles, performing extended leaps, and slipping through narrow spaces.

Their fur patterns and accessory choices reflect personal style and ingenuity. Their alert expressions and small, agile bodies convey intelligence, curiosity, and readiness. They rely on energy-rich foods and frequent rest to maintain vitality. Geisamahis are highly attuned to their environment, able to sense subtle dangers or hidden objects.

They possess natural dexterity for crafting, tinkering, or manipulating objects with ease. Their instincts guide them in navigation, problem-solving, and coordination with allies. They adapt easily to both natural and urban environments, finding creative solutions to challenges. Their movements are acrobatic and deliberate, blending efficiency with elegance.
They are inherently curious, inventive, and playful, always exploring, observing, and responding to the world around them.

They communicate through gestures, expressions, and subtle vocalizations, and their presence often conveys curiosity, mischief, or intelligence. Their culture emphasizes adaptability, invention, and self-reliance, and they often live in tight-knit groups that share knowledge and resources. Geisamahis are persistent problem-solvers, thriving in situations that demand cleverness or unconventional approaches. Their physical and mental traits are closely tied to their magical sustenance, making arcane energy and enchanted environments particularly vital to their well-being.

They are resourceful, inventive, and always seeking ways to outthink challenges or obstacles in their path. Geisamahis appear as upright, fur-covered creatures with large, expressive eyes and long whiskers that twitch in response to their surroundings. Their nimble hands and opposable thumbs allow them to handle tools, gadgets, or delicate objects with precision. They move quickly and lightly, capable of scaling obstacles, performing extended leaps, and slipping through narrow spaces.

Their fur patterns and accessory choices reflect personal style and ingenuity. Their alert expressions and small, agile bodies convey intelligence, curiosity, and readiness. They rely on energy-rich foods and frequent rest to maintain vitality. Geisamahis are highly attuned to their environment, able to sense subtle dangers or hidden objects.

They possess natural dexterity for crafting, tinkering, or manipulating objects with ease. Their instincts guide them in navigation, problem-solving, and coordination with allies. They adapt easily to both natural and urban environments, finding creative solutions to challenges. Their movements are acrobatic and deliberate, blending efficiency with elegance.
They are inherently curious, inventive, and playful, always exploring, observing, and responding to the world around them.

sections.heading: Geisamahi Traits
content: Your Geisamahi character has the following racial traits.
Ability Score Increase. Your Dexterity score increases by 2, and your Intelligence or Wisdom score increases by 1.
Creature Type. You are a Humanoid.
Size. You are Small.
Speed. Your base walking speed is 30 feet. You also have a climbing speed of 30 feet.
Nimble Body. You can move through the space of any creature that is at least one size larger than you. Squeezing through spaces large enough for a Small creature costs you no extra movement.

Keen Whiskers and Nose. You gain proficiency in Perception or Investigation. You have advantage on checks made to locate hidden passages, traps, small objects, relics, food, scents, tracks, or recent disturbances in cluttered terrain.

Tinker-Claws. You gain proficiency with thieves' tools, tinkerer's tools, or one artisan's tool of your choice. During a short rest, you may improvise a tiny device, wedge, hook, noisemaker, trip-cord, patch, or simple mechanism from scavenged materials. The device lasts until your next long rest or until used.

Acrobatic Dash. As a bonus action, you may Dash, Disengage, or climb without provoking opportunity attacks until the end of your turn. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

Coordinated Instinct. When an ally within 5 feet of you makes an ability check using a skill or tool you are proficient with, you may use your reaction to grant that ally a +1d4 bonus to the roll. You can use this trait once per short or long rest.
Languages. You can speak, read, and write Common and one additional language of your choice.

sections.heading: Classes I Point Players Toward
content: Rogue, Artificer, Ranger, Bard, Monk, Fighter, or any scout/tinker role.

sections.heading: Roleplaying Notes
content: Let the character's body language reflect their core concept: upright ferret- or stoat-like folk with quick hands, heightened senses, acrobatic movement, tool use, and relentless curiosity.
Tie daily needs, grooming, clothing, ritual practice, and social habits to the race's biology instead of treating traits as only combat powers.
I use the race's homeland, bloodline, environmental preference, and magical sustenance as hooks for settlement placement, NPC schedules, family traditions, and adventuring goals.
When a mechanical trait overlaps with a class feature, me as MOL should allow the player to choose the most flavorful option without stacking beyond the table's balance comfort.

sections.heading: MOL Notes for Universal Integration
content: This race is designed to plug into Universal settlements, NPC generators, regional biome logic, and ancestry-aware character creation. When assigning NPCs, prioritize habitats and cultures that match their physical needs and magical affinities.

sections.heading: Universal Alignment Profile
content: Typical race profile: Neutral Coordinator — A practical helper and team lead: problem-solving, supportive, and useful without demanding control.
Geisamahi are small ferretfolk tinkerers, scouts, and problem-solvers. Their culture rewards cleverness, shared work, practical fixes, and fast adaptation more than heavy lawfulness.

MOL use: Use Geisamahi as gadget scouts, tunnel couriers, clockwork assistants, trapwrights, and workshop families. Criminal crews can drop toward Neutral Knave; guild-focused clans can climb toward Lawful Coordinator.

blocks.text: Dragonborn
A player-facing race guide I use as MOL for Universal.

Created by: Valkhamesh. I present this race as created by Valkhamesh only. Other powers can appear as patrons, rivals, temples, bargains, or local traditions, but they are not creator gods for this race.
My table category: Draconic and Reptilian Races.
My table classification: I place Dragonborn with Draconic and Reptilian Races, with each Dragonborn lineage inheriting moderated abilities from its Universal dragon parentage.
Universal Alignment System Summary

Universal treats alignment as a living profile instead of a fixed label. Every dragon or Dragonborn lineage can be described through four independent axes from 0 to 3000, with 1500 as the neutral center.
Phase ranges: 0-999 extreme negative; 1000-1499 skewed negative; 1500 true neutral; 1501-1999 skewed positive; 2000-3000 extreme positive.
What I Tell My Players

Dragonborns are descendants of the homebrew and the elemental draconic bloodlines that shaped civilizations, skies, mountains, seas, forests, deserts, and hidden magical sites across Universal. They retain scaled skin, powerful tails, wings, clawed hands, facial ridges, and an unmistakable humanoid-dragonoid posture.

this version makes the parentage rule explicit: every homebrew Dragonborn lineage has the abilities of its Universal dragon parentage. A lineage does not borrow default D&D dragon traits unless me as MOL chooses to add them. Its magic comes from the listed Universal parent dragons.

Alignment is not fixed by ancestry. Each lineage has a suggested starting profile based on cultural pattern, habitat, and inherited magic. Individual Dragonborn can shift along all four axes through choices, vows, betrayals, sacrifices, faction pressure, and personal growth.
Dragonborn Traits
Parentage Inheritance Rule

Every lineage below lists its Universal dragon parentage and converts those dragon abilities into playable racial features. If a lineage names multiple dragons, it represents a blended or culturally recognized parentage. The Dragonborn inherits the power themes from all named parents, but the mechanical expression is moderated for a player character.

Suggested alignment scores are starting cultural tendencies only. They are useful for NPC generation, settlement logic, family expectations, and faction reactions, but they do not restrict player choice.
Lineage Crosswalk
Dragonborn Lineages
Noitzideq - Air and Weather
Dragon parentage: Asaafi + Sauqonsex, with Boisein storm influence
Inherited ability theme: Sky, weather, air/wind, storm movement, and healing currents.
Suggested Universal alignment profile: Neutral Coordinator
Parentage abilities:
Resistance: choose lightning or thunder after each long rest.
Wind Rider: PB/long rest, bonus action until end of turn; +10 ft movement and ignore wind, storm, grass, and open-air difficult terrain.
Sky-Healer Current: starting at 3rd level, once per long rest you can heal a creature you touch for 1d6 + PB, or push/pull a willing creature 10 feet with a harmless gust.
Weather Sense: advantage on checks to predict natural weather, read clouds, or navigate open sky.
Classes I point players toward: Ranger, Cleric, Druid, Monk, Storm Sorcerer, Paladin

How I guide roleplaying: Let this lineage's body language, daily needs, grooming, favored homes, and social expectations reflect its dragon parentage. The same inherited power may become protective, selfish, lawful, chaotic, honorable, or pragmatic depending on actual play.
Saelftum - Volcanic Flame
Dragon parentage: Erymasos + Oreilhya, with Zrom elemental pressure
Inherited ability theme: Fire, heat, molten resilience, temperature control, and volcanic endurance.
Suggested Universal alignment profile: Lawful Defender
Parentage abilities:
Resistance: fire damage.
Molten Body: you are adapted to extreme heat and can shed dim molten light in a 10-foot radius.
Heat Command: PB/long rest, as an action you intensify or dampen nonmagical heat/flame in a 10-foot space, or deal fire damage equal to PB to a creature you can see within 30 feet.
Volcanic Reprisal: once per long rest when you take fire damage, reduce it by your level + PB and your next melee hit before the end of your next turn deals extra fire damage equal to PB.
Classes I point players toward: Barbarian, Fighter, Paladin, Forge Cleric, Sorcerer, Artificer

How I guide roleplaying: Let this lineage's body language, daily needs, grooming, favored homes, and social expectations reflect its dragon parentage. The same inherited power may become protective, selfish, lawful, chaotic, honorable, or pragmatic depending on actual play.
Jazwed - Lava and Crystal
Dragon parentage: Erymasos + Nenshexeq + Zrom
Inherited ability theme: Fire, stone, crystal force, elemental shaping, and defensive engineering.
Suggested Universal alignment profile: Lawful Enforcer
Parentage abilities:
Resistance: fire damage.
Crystal-Lava Strike: once on each of your turns when you hit with an unarmed strike or melee weapon attack, add PB bludgeoning or fire damage.
Thermal Crystal Sight: advantage on checks to detect recent heat, magma vents, forged objects, or unstable stone within 30 feet.
Elemental Masonry: PB/long rest, shape loose stone, crystal, cooled lava, or packed earth in a 5-foot cube into cover, steps, a brace, or a rough barrier.
Classes I point players toward: Fighter, Artificer, Barbarian, Paladin, Rune Knight, War Wizard

How I guide roleplaying: Let this lineage's body language, daily needs, grooming, favored homes, and social expectations reflect its dragon parentage. The same inherited power may become protective, selfish, lawful, chaotic, honorable, or pragmatic depending on actual play.
Khoalaros - Tide and Ocean
Dragon parentage: Philous + Xuqhuath + Yichah
Inherited ability theme: Sea control, water shaping, currents, swimming grace, aquatic communication, and healing water.
Suggested Universal alignment profile: Neutral Guardian
Parentage abilities:
Movement: swimming speed equal to walking speed; you can hold your breath for 1 hour, or breathe water if me as MOL wants full aquatic parentage.
Current Rider: ignore nonmagical movement penalties from currents, reefs, kelp, mudflats, and shallow coastal terrain.
Marine Speech: communicate simple concepts to aquatic beasts and water spirits.
Healing Tide: starting at 3rd level, once per long rest you can touch a creature with water or mist to restore 1d6 + PB hit points or end one nonmagical choking/drowning effect.
Classes I point players toward: Druid, Tempest Cleric, Ranger, Bard, Fathomless Warlock, Sorcerer

How I guide roleplaying: Let this lineage's body language, daily needs, grooming, favored homes, and social expectations reflect its dragon parentage. The same inherited power may become protective, selfish, lawful, chaotic, honorable, or pragmatic depending on actual play.

Taudinax - Shadow and Light
Dragon parentage: Ekhoq + Pteris + Xacuacsih/Thusekha, with Kiczi illusion influence
Inherited ability theme: Shadow manipulation, darkness, illusion, tactical concealment, and controlled light.
Suggested Universal alignment profile: Neutral Strategist
Parentage abilities:
Skill: proficiency in Stealth.
Minor Illusion: you know the minor illusion cantrip.
Mist-and-Shadow Hide: in dim light, darkness, fog, dense forest, swamp mist, or heavy shadow, you may Hide while lightly obscured.

Shadow-Light Veil: PB/long rest, as an action you dim, brighten, color, or distort light in a 10-foot area for 1 minute; creatures of your choice can gain advantage on one Stealth or Performance check while inside it.
Classes I point players toward: Rogue, Warlock, Ranger, Illusion Wizard, Shadow Monk, Bard

How I guide roleplaying: Let this lineage's body language, daily needs, grooming, favored homes, and social expectations reflect its dragon parentage. The same inherited power may become protective, selfish, lawful, chaotic, honorable, or pragmatic depending on actual play.
Gouxelq - Metal and Crystal
Dragon parentage: Aloic + Nenshexeq + Zrom
Inherited ability theme: Metal control, stone/crystal shaping, elemental structure, and crafted barriers.
Suggested Universal alignment profile: Lawful Coordinator
Parentage abilities:
Tool Gift: proficiency with smith's tools, mason's tools, or jeweler's tools.
Material Reading: as an action, touch nonmagical metal, stone, or crystal and learn whether it is natural, forged, hollow, fractured, or magically altered.
Crystal Brace: PB/long rest, create a short-lived brace, wedge, shield ridge, or 5-foot partial barrier from nearby mineral, stone, or metal fragments.
Metal Resonance: advantage on checks to appraise, repair, identify, or sabotage metal and crystal structures.
Classes I point players toward: Artificer, Fighter, Forge Cleric, Wizard, Paladin, Rune Knight

How I guide roleplaying: Let this lineage's body language, daily needs, grooming, favored homes, and social expectations reflect its dragon parentage. The same inherited power may become protective, selfish, lawful, chaotic, honorable, or pragmatic depending on actual play.
Vautaces - Radiance and Foresight
Dragon parentage: Thusekha + Xacuacsih + Mumh + Lunngha/Eecors + Chiellieds
Inherited ability theme: Light control, radiant protection, perception, foresight, time-sense, and emotional insight.
Suggested Universal alignment profile: Lawful Arbiter
Parentage abilities:
Skill: proficiency in Insight or Arcana.
Guiding Flash: PB/long rest, when you or a creature you can see within 30 feet makes an ability check or saving throw, add 1d4 after seeing the d20 but before knowing the outcome.
Radiant Sense: you know the light cantrip; your light may appear as ruby, cream, gold, or star-white radiance.
Foresight Pulse: starting at 5th level, once per long rest you may briefly read a pattern in fate, gaining advantage on one Insight, Arcana, Perception, or initiative roll.
Classes I point players toward: Wizard, Cleric, Sorcerer, Paladin, Bard, Divination Wizard

How I guide roleplaying: Let this lineage's body language, daily needs, grooming, favored homes, and social expectations reflect its dragon parentage. The same inherited power may become protective, selfish, lawful, chaotic, honorable, or pragmatic depending on actual play.

path: Dragonborn Alignment Use at the Table
blocks.text: For PC Dragonborn, start from the lineage score if the player wants a culture-shaped default. Otherwise begin at 1500 on every axis and shift only where the backstory clearly justifies it.

path: Dragonborn Alignment Use at the Table
blocks.text: For NPC Dragonborn, use the lineage profile to place them in settlements and factions. Noitzideq, Khoalaros, Gouxelq, and Vautaces often function well in organized civic roles; Taudinax often fit scouts, spies, and hidden guardians; Saelftum, Jazwed, and Tuorszom often fit industrial, martial, volcanic, or mountain societies; Gauksneth fit desert oases, caravans, and resource guilds.

path: Dragonborn Alignment Use at the Table
blocks.text: Lineage abilities should remain Universal-specific. A Saelftum Dragonborn inherits heat and volcanic fire from Erymasos and Oreilhya; a Khoalaros inherits sea, water, and healing themes from Philous, Xuqhuath, and Yichah; a Taudinax inherits shadow, illusion, and light from Ekhoq, Pteris, and silver-light parentage.
MOL Notes for Balance

If a lineage feature overlaps with a class feature, let the player choose the most flavorful version without stacking beyond your table comfort. Parentage features are meant to express ancestry, not outshine class identity.

When granting additional parentage powers through story, use alignment consequences. A dragon ancestor may withhold deeper gifts from a descendant whose choices violate its own profile, or may awaken stronger magic when a descendant makes a defining vow, sacrifice, betrayal, or redemption.

sections.heading: Dragonborn Alignment Use at the Table
path: Dragonborn Alignment Use at the Table
content: For PC Dragonborn, start from the lineage score if the player wants a culture-shaped default. Otherwise begin at 1500 on every axis and shift only where the backstory clearly justifies it.

For NPC Dragonborn, use the lineage profile to place them in settlements and factions. Noitzideq, Khoalaros, Gouxelq, and Vautaces often function well in organized civic roles; Taudinax often fit scouts, spies, and hidden guardians; Saelftum, Jazwed, and Tuorszom often fit industrial, martial, volcanic, or mountain societies; Gauksneth fit desert oases, caravans, and resource guilds.

Lineage abilities should remain Universal-specific. A Saelftum Dragonborn inherits heat and volcanic fire from Erymasos and Oreilhya; a Khoalaros inherits sea, water, and healing themes from Philous, Xuqhuath, and Yichah; a Taudinax inherits shadow, illusion, and light from Ekhoq, Pteris, and silver-light parentage.

sections.heading: MOL Notes for Balance
content: If a lineage feature overlaps with a class feature, let the player choose the most flavorful version without stacking beyond your table comfort. Parentage features are meant to express ancestry, not outshine class identity.

When granting additional parentage powers through story, use alignment consequences. A dragon ancestor may withhold deeper gifts from a descendant whose choices violate its own profile, or may awaken stronger magic when a descendant makes a defining vow, sacrifice, betrayal, or redemption.

rows: Increase one ability score by 2 and another ability score by 1, or increase three different ability scores by 1 each.
You are a Humanoid with draconic ancestry.
Your base walking speed is 30 feet.
You can see in dim light within 60 feet as if it were bright light, and darkness as if it were dim light. You cannot discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

You have scaled skin, claws, a powerful tail, and facial ridges tied to your bloodline. Your claws are natural weapons that deal 1d6 slashing damage. You also have advantage on ability checks or saving throws made to keep your balance.

Your wings are part of your natural body. When you fall and are not incapacitated, you may use your reaction to reduce falling damage by an amount equal to five times your level. Starting at 5th level, you may fly for 1 minute at a flying speed equal to your walking speed. Once you use this flight, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

Choose one Dragonborn lineage. You gain its parentage ability package. When a lineage ability requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution, Wisdom, or Charisma modifier, chosen when you select this race.
You gain proficiency in one of the following skills: Arcana, History, Intimidation, Nature, Perception, or Religion.
You can speak, read, and write Common and Draconic.

races.name: Panolima
races.summary: Living Embodiments of Elemental Harmony: Earth, Fire, Water, Air, and Aether. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.
player_lore: The Panolimas are beings of elemental harmony . Their bodies are infused with one of the five primordial elemental threads: Earth, Fire, Water, Air, or Aether. Each individual exhibits physical traits reflecting their elemental affinity, from stone-like skin and mossy hair to flowing, water-like forms or luminous, energy-filled auras. They thrive in environments aligned with their element, drawing sustenance, vitality, and energy from landscapes, currents, storms, magma, or ley lines.

Their movements, gestures, and even voices often carry the rhythm of their element, and they engage in ritual cleansing or meditation to maintain harmony with their elemental thread. Earth Panolimas have skin patterned like bark or stone, hair resembling moss or soil, and a deep-toned, rumbling voice. They require contact with solid terrain, forests, caves, or mountains to maintain vitality. Their abilities include sensing structural weaknesses, reinforcing the land, and enduring physical hardships with exceptional resilience.

They can read terrain, detect mineral-rich soils, and manipulate stone or plant life to shape their surroundings. Fire Panolimas exhibit cracks like magma across their skin, ember-red hair, and glowing eyes. They rely on heat sources, volcanic activity, and exposure to flames to sustain energy. Their bodies radiate warmth and light, and they can manipulate molten materials, summon bursts of flame, and purify areas through fire.

They often engage in rituals involving forging, combat, or controlled burns to maintain their vitality. Water Panolimas have fluid, reflective skin textures, hair like flowing water, and eyes resembling lakes or oceans. They thrive in rivers, lakes, oceans, or glacial regions and maintain hydration and strength through immersion in water. Their abilities allow them to manipulate currents, swim with exceptional speed, shape water barriers, and harmonize with aquatic life.

Ritual bathing and communion with water are central to their well-being and spiritual balance. Air Panolimas are marked by cloud-like hair, shifting skin patterns, and luminous, sky-toned eyes. They require open skies, high-altitude plains, or exposure to winds to maintain health and focus. Their bodies are naturally light and mobile, enabling gliding, control of air currents, and swift, graceful movement.

They are attuned to storms, pressure changes, and wind-borne sounds, often performing aerial rituals to restore vitality. Aether Panolimas have skin infused with living energy, hair that flows with raw elemental light, and glowing patterns that shift with their mood. They draw strength from ley lines, arcane storms, and areas of concentrated magical energy. Their abilities include channeling ambient energy, enhancing magical flow, sensing mystical currents, and manipulating arcane forces in their environment.

Meditation, spellcasting, and exposure to elemental convergence maintain their vitality and focus. All Panolimas share a deep connection to their elemental thread, shaping their culture, movements, diet, and environmental needs. They live in harmony with their surroundings, performing rituals and meditative practices to sustain energy and maintain balance. Their bodies physically and spiritually reflect the pulse of their element, and they are capable of interacting with the world in ways that extend beyond the purely physical.

They are attuned to the subtle flows of energy in the environment, able to sense dangers, currents, and opportunities through elemental perception. Their appearance is highly variable but always marked by the integration of elemental traits with humanoid form. Every Panolimas carries a rhythm of life that echoes the essence of their thread, from the motion of their limbs to the tone of their voice. Rituals, elemental communion, and environmental attunement are essential for their survival.

Their presence often shapes their surroundings, subtly harmonizing or enhancing the elemental qualities of the places they inhabit. They reproduce either naturally or through magical means, passing on their elemental affinity to their progeny. Their society values balance, unity, and integration with the natural and mystical worlds. Panolimas serve as living embodiments of elemental harmony, blending culture, body, and environment into a single, flowing pulse of life.

Earth Bloodline: Earth Panolimas are grounded in forests, mountains, and caves, drawing strength from stone and soil. Their bark-like skin and mossy hair allow them to blend with natural terrain. They can sense structural weaknesses, manipulate plants and minerals, and endure harsh physical conditions. Their voices carry a deep, resonant tone reflecting the heartbeat of the land.

Rituals often involve shaping stone or connecting with sacred groves. Fire Bloodline: Fire Panolimas have glowing skin with magma-like cracks and ember-red hair. blocks.text: Panolima
A player-facing race guide I use as MOL for Universal.
Created by: Horundar. I present this race as created by Horundar only. Other powers can appear as patrons, rivals, temples, bargains, or local traditions, but they are not creator gods for this race.
My table category: Elemental and Energy-Born Peoples.
Living Embodiments of Elemental Harmony: Earth, Fire, Water, Air, and Aether
What I Tell My Players

The Panolimas are beings of elemental harmony . Their bodies are infused with one of the five primordial elemental threads: Earth, Fire, Water, Air, or Aether. Each individual exhibits physical traits reflecting their elemental affinity, from stone-like skin and mossy hair to flowing, water-like forms or luminous, energy-filled auras. They thrive in environments aligned with their element, drawing sustenance, vitality, and energy from landscapes, currents, storms, magma, or ley lines.

Their movements, gestures, and even voices often carry the rhythm of their element, and they engage in ritual cleansing or meditation to maintain harmony with their elemental thread. Earth Panolimas have skin patterned like bark or stone, hair resembling moss or soil, and a deep-toned, rumbling voice. They require contact with solid terrain, forests, caves, or mountains to maintain vitality. Their abilities include sensing structural weaknesses, reinforcing the land, and enduring physical hardships with exceptional resilience.

They can read terrain, detect mineral-rich soils, and manipulate stone or plant life to shape their surroundings. Fire Panolimas exhibit cracks like magma across their skin, ember-red hair, and glowing eyes. They rely on heat sources, volcanic activity, and exposure to flames to sustain energy. Their bodies radiate warmth and light, and they can manipulate molten materials, summon bursts of flame, and purify areas through fire.

They often engage in rituals involving forging, combat, or controlled burns to maintain their vitality. Water Panolimas have fluid, reflective skin textures, hair like flowing water, and eyes resembling lakes or oceans. They thrive in rivers, lakes, oceans, or glacial regions and maintain hydration and strength through immersion in water. Their abilities allow them to manipulate currents, swim with exceptional speed, shape water barriers, and harmonize with aquatic life.

Ritual bathing and communion with water are central to their well-being and spiritual balance. Air Panolimas are marked by cloud-like hair, shifting skin patterns, and luminous, sky-toned eyes. They require open skies, high-altitude plains, or exposure to winds to maintain health and focus. Their bodies are naturally light and mobile, enabling gliding, control of air currents, and swift, graceful movement.

They are attuned to storms, pressure changes, and wind-borne sounds, often performing aerial rituals to restore vitality. Aether Panolimas have skin infused with living energy, hair that flows with raw elemental light, and glowing patterns that shift with their mood. They draw strength from ley lines, arcane storms, and areas of concentrated magical energy. Their abilities include channeling ambient energy, enhancing magical flow, sensing mystical currents, and manipulating arcane forces in their environment.

Meditation, spellcasting, and exposure to elemental convergence maintain their vitality and focus. All Panolimas share a deep connection to their elemental thread, shaping their culture, movements, diet, and environmental needs. They live in harmony with their surroundings, performing rituals and meditative practices to sustain energy and maintain balance. Their bodies physically and spiritually reflect the pulse of their element, and they are capable of interacting with the world in ways that extend beyond the purely physical.

They are attuned to the subtle flows of energy in the environment, able to sense dangers, currents, and opportunities through elemental perception. Their appearance is highly variable but always marked by the integration of elemental traits with humanoid form. Every Panolimas carries a rhythm of life that echoes the essence of their thread, from the motion of their limbs to the tone of their voice. Rituals, elemental communion, and environmental attunement are essential for their survival.

Their presence often shapes their surroundings, subtly harmonizing or enhancing the elemental qualities of the places they inhabit. They reproduce either naturally or through magical means, passing on their elemental affinity to their progeny. Their society values balance, unity, and integration with the natural and mystical worlds. Panolimas serve as living embodiments of elemental harmony, blending culture, body, and environment into a single, flowing pulse of life.

They can manipulate ambient energy, sense mystical currents, and enhance magical flow. Their rituals involve meditation, spell attunement, and interaction with arcane forces.
They appear luminous and otherworldly, often leaving traces of energy in their wake.
