Often associated with structured societies and formal magical education. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

subtypes.name: Wood Elf
subtypes.canonical_description: Reclusive, nature-bound elves who live in forests and wildlands. They are swift, perceptive, and deeply attuned to natural ecosystems and survival. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

subtypes.name: Drow (Underdark Elf)
subtypes.canonical_description: Dark-reflection elves who dwell beneath the surface world in vast subterranean realms. Often shaped by harsh theocratic societies, they are known for their affinity with shadow, spider symbolism, and survival in the Underdark. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

subtypes.name: Eladrin
subtypes.canonical_description: Fey-touched elves whose emotions and magical expressions shift with the seasons or emotional states. They are closely tied to the Feywild and its ever-changing nature. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

subtypes.name: Astral Elf
subtypes.canonical_description: Originating from the Astral Plane or cosmic realms beyond mortal understanding, astral elves carry a starborne perspective and innate connection to psychic and stellar magic. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

subtypes.name: Sea Elf
subtypes.canonical_description: Aquatic elves adapted to life beneath the waves. They thrive in oceanic environments, maintaining deep cultural ties to marine ecosystems, reef civilizations, and seafaring alliances. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

subtypes.name: Shadar-Kai
subtypes.canonical_description: Shadow-bound elves tied to bleak or shadowy realms, often serving powerful entities of the Shadowfell. They are hardened, disciplined, and resilient due to their exposure to despair and entropy. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

subtypes.name: Pallid Elf
subtypes.canonical_description: Pale, fey-marked elves often associated with luminous or uncanny wilderness regions. They tend to be curious, observant, and subtly otherworldly in demeanor. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

subtypes.name: Star Elf (Lunar/Heavenly)
subtypes.canonical_description: Elves touched by celestial cycles or moonlit magic, often interpreting fate and emotion through lunar phases and astral influence. They are commonly linked with prophecy, dreams, and night magic. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

subtypes.name: Avariel (Winged Elf)
subtypes.canonical_description: Rare winged elves capable of flight, often dwelling in isolated sky-bound enclaves or mountainous aeries. They are proud, reclusive, and deeply tied to freedom and aerial mastery. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

subtypes.name: Snow Elf (Frostbound)
subtypes.canonical_description: Elves adapted to arctic or glacial regions, shaped by endurance, isolation, and survival in harsh cold environments. They often carry traditions centered on resilience and ancestral memory. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

subtypes.name: Sun Elf
subtypes.canonical_description: Radiant and disciplined elves often associated with daylight, order, and structured magical traditions. They emphasize perfection, heritage, and arcane mastery. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

subtypes.name: Moon Elf
subtypes.canonical_description: Flexible and wandering elves often more open to other cultures, adventure, and change. They balance arcane affinity with emotional adaptability and curiosity. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

subtypes.name: Shadowmoor Elf
subtypes.canonical_description: Elves shaped by lands of perpetual gloom and magical distortion. They develop survivalist instincts, cautious worldviews, and resilience in unstable magical environments. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

subtypes.name: Celestial Elf
subtypes.canonical_description: Elves touched directly by divine or heavenly forces, often serving as emissaries, guardians, or chosen vessels of higher powers. They radiate an innate sense of grace, protection, and sacred purpose. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.

races.canonical_parent_description: Elves are long-lived, graceful beings deeply attuned to magic, nature, and art. Their societies often value tradition, beauty, and refined mastery of specialized skills. They are broadly divided across many cultural and biological lineages throughout the worlds of the multiverse. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.

races.name: Kaluseban
races.classification: I place Kaluseban as an Elf bloodline under the Elf parent race.
races.summary: Elegant Mana-Bound Humanoids of Ley Lines, Nature, Moonlight, and Shadow. Kaluseban is a separate parent race from Elf.
player_lore: Kalusebans are an elegant and enigmatic race of magical humanoids . They are tall and slender, with graceful features and skin tones that reflect their bloodline, ranging from pale ivory to deep sapphire or earthy greens and browns. Their eyes often glow faintly, carrying hues tied to their magical affinity, and their hair can shimmer, float slightly, or reflect celestial or natural motifs. Kalusebans carry an aura of otherworldly presence, appearing almost ethereal as if the ambient magic bends subtly around them.

They thrive in environments rich with mana, nature, or celestial energy, and their forms are highly sensitive to ritual, lunar phases, and environmental harmony. Kalusebans require periodic exposure to magical energy, whether through ley lines, enchanted sites, or ceremonial practices, to maintain their vitality and arcane strength. They bond strongly with natural environments, finding balance and clarity among forests, rivers, or sacred groves. Rituals, music, meditation, or alignment with celestial bodies enhance their mental and emotional equilibrium.

Deprivation from magic, polluted areas, or urban confines can weaken their vitality, induce restlessness, or diminish their magical attunement. They also maintain basic needs like nutrition, hydration, and hygiene, often observing these through symbolic or ceremonial acts that reinforce cultural traditions. Kalusebans have abilities tied to their bloodline and affinity. They can manipulate natural or arcane energies, commune with flora and fauna, sense ley lines or currents of magical energy, and subtly influence the environment around them.

Some can breathe or move through water, sense tides, or manipulate mist and fog. Others are attuned to shadows, illusions, or subterranean energies, using these senses to navigate or protect sacred spaces. Many can channel magic into physical objects or inscriptions, embedding power into runes, wards, or glyphs. Their reflexes, agility, and awareness are enhanced in environments that correspond to their affinity, and their connection to lunar or celestial phases amplifies certain abilities.

They can also perceive psychic or dream-like patterns, granting insight into others’ intentions or the echoes of the past. Across all bloodlines, Kalusebans maintain a deep respect for balance, using their abilities to heal, guide, or preserve rather than dominate. Arcane Kalusebans are characterized by luminous skin in shades of gold, ivory, or deep violet, with glowing eyes and hands that often pulse with magical energy. Their forms are regal and poised, and they favor robes or garments decorated with runes and glyphs that shimmer with stored mana.

They are drawn to ley lines, libraries, and magical sites, where they can weave spells, inscribe runes, and study arcane knowledge. Their presence subtly enhances ambient magic, and they can channel power into objects or rituals. Arcane Kalusebans possess a natural resilience to mental manipulation or illusions, and their thinking is often methodical, analytical, and attuned to cosmic patterns. Starborne Kalusebans have pale blue, silver, or amethyst skin that glows faintly under moonlight, with hair that flows like moonlight and eyes reflecting celestial motifs.

Their forms are ethereal, often appearing weightless or luminous in darkness. They are attuned to lunar phases and celestial alignments, which influence their abilities and perception. Starborne Kalusebans are sensitive to psychic and dream-like patterns, capable of reading intentions or seeing glimpses of possible futures. They often act as seers, dream interpreters, or guides, connecting mortal and mystical realms.

Wildroot Kalusebans exhibit earthy skin tones with bark-like textures, vine-wrapped limbs, or leaf-patterned markings that blend with forests. Their hair may resemble flowing grasses or moss, and their eyes reflect the shades of foliage or animal patterns. They are attuned to flora, fauna, and elemental terrains, sensing natural energies and communicating subtly with animals or plants. Their presence encourages growth and regeneration in natural environments, and they can harness elemental forces like storms or soil movement.

Wildroot Kalusebans are instinctive and adaptive, moving with agility through forests and wilderness. Tideborn Kalusebans have iridescent skin with pearl-blue, aquamarine, or dusky hues, hair that drifts like underwater currents, and eyes that resemble deep seas. Their forms may show subtle aquatic traits, such as webbed fingers or gill-like markings. They are naturally attuned to water, tides, and mist, able to perceive currents, manipulate moisture, and move gracefully through aquatic environments.

Tideborn Kalusebans sense the memory of waters, gaining insight from oceans, rivers, and coastal areas. Their presence can affect the flow of local waters, summon fog or mist, and influence aquatic life. Stonebound Kalusebans possess skin in granite, sandstone, or muted moonstone tones with crystalline highlights, and markings etched like runes along limbs or torso. Their hair may shimmer like mineral veins, and their eyes often reflect earthy hues.

They are attuned to stone, minerals, and subterranean spaces, sensing shifts in the earth and resonances in rock. Stonebound Kalusebans can channel energy into protective wards or manipulate terrain for stability or concealment. Their movements are deliberate and grounded, and their endurance is heightened in rocky or mineral-rich environments. Umbral Kalusebans have dark, shadowed skin with phosphorescent veins, engraved runes, and eyes that may display shifting symbols.

Their forms favor concealment, often draped in dark or muted clothing that enhances their silent movements. They are attuned to shadows, subterranean spaces, and illusions, able to perceive through darkness and manipulate perception. Umbral Kalusebans excel at stealth, observation, and subtle influence, and their presence can distort light or sound. They often serve as guardians of hidden paths or secret knowledge, moving unseen and affecting the environment with minimal disturbance.

They can manipulate natural or arcane energies, commune with flora and fauna, sense ley lines or currents of magical energy, and subtly influence the environment around them.

Some can breathe or move through water, sense tides, or manipulate mist and fog. Others are attuned to shadows, illusions, or subterranean energies, using these senses to navigate or protect sacred spaces. Many can channel magic into physical objects or inscriptions, embedding power into runes, wards, or glyphs. Their reflexes, agility, and awareness are enhanced in environments that correspond to their affinity, and their connection to lunar or celestial phases amplifies certain abilities.

They can also perceive psychic or dream-like patterns, granting insight into others’ intentions or the echoes of the past. Across all bloodlines, Kalusebans maintain a deep respect for balance, using their abilities to heal, guide, or preserve rather than dominate. Arcane Kalusebans are characterized by luminous skin in shades of gold, ivory, or deep violet, with glowing eyes and hands that often pulse with magical energy. Their forms are regal and poised, and they favor robes or garments decorated with runes and glyphs that shimmer with stored mana.

They are drawn to ley lines, libraries, and magical sites, where they can weave spells, inscribe runes, and study arcane knowledge. Their presence subtly enhances ambient magic, and they can channel power into objects or rituals. Arcane Kalusebans possess a natural resilience to mental manipulation or illusions, and their thinking is often methodical, analytical, and attuned to cosmic patterns. Psionic Kalusebans have pale blue, silver, or amethyst skin that glows faintly under moonlight, with hair that flows like moonlight and eyes reflecting celestial motifs.

Their forms are ethereal, often appearing weightless or luminous in darkness. They are attuned to lunar phases and celestial alignments, which influence their abilities and perception. Psionic Kalusebans are sensitive to psychic and dream-like patterns, capable of reading intentions or seeing glimpses of possible futures. They often act as seers, dream interpreters, or guides, connecting mortal and mystical realms.

Swamp Kalusebans exhibit earthy skin tones with bark-like textures, vine-wrapped limbs, or leaf-patterned markings that blend with forests. Their hair may resemble flowing grasses or moss, and their eyes reflect the shades of foliage or animal patterns. They are attuned to flora, fauna, and elemental terrains, sensing natural energies and communicating subtly with animals or plants. Their presence encourages growth and regeneration in natural environments, and they can harness elemental forces like storms or soil movement.

Swamp Kalusebans are instinctive and adaptive, moving with agility through forests and wilderness. Oceanic Kalusebans have iridescent skin with pearl-blue, aquamarine, or dusky hues, hair that drifts like underwater currents, and eyes that resemble deep seas. Their forms may show subtle aquatic traits, such as webbed fingers or gill-like markings. They are naturally attuned to water, tides, and mist, able to perceive currents, manipulate moisture, and move gracefully through aquatic environments.

Oceanic Kalusebans sense the memory of waters, gaining insight from oceans, rivers, and coastal areas. Their presence can affect the flow of local waters, summon fog or mist, and influence aquatic life. Stone Kalusebans possess skin in granite, sandstone, or muted moonstone tones with crystalline highlights, and markings etched like runes along limbs or torso. Their hair may shimmer like mineral veins, and their eyes often reflect earthy hues.

They are attuned to stone, minerals, and subterranean spaces, sensing shifts in the earth and resonances in rock. Stone Kalusebans can channel energy into protective wards or manipulate terrain for stability or concealment. Their movements are deliberate and grounded, and their endurance is heightened in rocky or mineral-rich environments. Dark Kalusebans have dark, shadowed skin with phosphorescent veins, engraved runes, and eyes that may display shifting symbols.

Their forms favor concealment, often draped in dark or muted clothing that enhances their silent movements. They are attuned to shadows, subterranean spaces, and illusions, able to perceive through darkness and manipulate perception. Dark Kalusebans excel at stealth, observation, and subtle influence, and their presence can distort light or sound. They often serve as guardians of hidden paths or secret knowledge, moving unseen and affecting the environment with minimal disturbance.

sections.heading: Kaluseban Traits
content: Your Kaluseban character has the following racial traits.
Ability Score Increase. Increase one ability score by 2 and another ability score by 1, or increase three different ability scores by 1 each.
Creature Type. You are a Humanoid.
Size. You are Medium.
Speed. Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

Mana-Bound Vitality. You require periodic exposure to magical energy, sacred natural sites, ley lines, celestial light, ritual practice, or enchanted environments to remain fully balanced. Long-term deprivation from magic may cause exhaustion, restlessness, or diminished spellcasting at me as MOL's discretion.

Leyline Sense. You gain proficiency in Arcana or Nature. You can sense whether a place has strong natural, celestial, arcane, shadow, aquatic, or earthen magical resonance after spending 1 minute in quiet focus.

Subtle Channeling. You know one cantrip of your choice from the druid, cleric, or wizard spell list. Wisdom, Intelligence, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for it, chosen when you select this race.
Ritual Poise. You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed by illusions, dream effects, or magic that distorts your perception of reality.
Bloodline Affinity. Choose one Kaluseban bloodline. You gain the bloodline gift listed for it.
Languages. You can speak, read, and write Common and one additional language tied to your home culture, bloodline, or magical tradition.

sections.heading: Bloodlines and Lineages
content: Choose one of the following Kaluseban bloodlines or lineages unless me as MOL allows mixed ancestry.

You know prestidigitation. At 3rd level, you may cast detect magic once per long rest. At 5th level, you may cast magic weapon or arcane lock once per long rest. Your chosen spellcasting ability for these spells is Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma.

You know guidance. At 3rd level, you may cast sleep once per long rest. At 5th level, you may cast augury once per long rest. You have advantage on checks made to interpret dreams, omens, lunar phases, or celestial alignments.

You know druidcraft. At 3rd level, you may cast speak with animals once per long rest. At 5th level, you may cast lesser restoration once per long rest. You can communicate simple emotional concepts to plants and beasts.

You gain a swimming speed equal to your walking speed and can breathe air and water. You know shape water. At 3rd level, you may cast fog cloud once per long rest. At 5th level, you may cast misty step once per long rest, appearing as mist or spray.

You gain proficiency in mason's tools or Religion. You know mold earth. At 3rd level, you may cast shield once per long rest. At 5th level, you may cast warding bond once per long rest without material components.
You gain darkvision out to 60 feet. You know minor illusion. At 3rd level, you may cast disguise self once per long rest. At 5th level, you may cast darkness once per long rest.

content: Druid, Wizard, Cleric, Warlock, Bard, Ranger, Sorcerer, or any ritual-focused class.

sections.heading: Roleplaying Notes
content: Let the character's body language reflect their core concept: ethereal magical humanoids whose bodies and minds rely on ambient magic, ritual harmony, and bloodline affinity.
Tie daily needs, grooming, clothing, ritual practice, and social habits to the race's biology instead of treating traits as only combat powers.
I use the race's homeland, bloodline, environmental preference, and magical sustenance as hooks for settlement placement, NPC schedules, family traditions, and adventuring goals.
When a mechanical trait overlaps with a class feature, me as MOL should allow the player to choose the most flavorful option without stacking beyond the table's balance comfort.

sections.heading: MOL Notes for Universal Integration
content: This race is designed to plug into Universal settlements, NPC generators, regional biome logic, and ancestry-aware character creation. When assigning NPCs, prioritize habitats and cultures that match their physical needs and magical affinities.

sections.heading: Universal Alignment Profile
content: Typical race profile: Neutral Arbiter — A watcher of balance and need: neither law-bound nor reckless, serving harmony and fairness as each situation demands.
Kaluseban are elegant mana-bound humanoids tied to ley lines, nature, moonlight, shadow, ritual, and bloodline variation. Their profile should emphasize balance, judgment, and magical responsibility.

MOL use: Use Kaluseban as ley-line stewards, moonlit wardens, arcane diplomats, shadow-blooded guides, and ritual arbiters. Individual bloodlines can adjust the axis scores: umbral lower lawfulness, starborne higher honor, wildroot higher altruism.

races.name: Gandirosha
races.summary: Luck-Touched Wanderers of Charm, Timing, and Subtle Magic. Temple marginalia marks this as a tuned lineage expression rather than a separate act of mercy.
player_lore: Gandiroshas are a race of magical, agile beings . Their presence in Universal is defined by charm, intuition, and a deep attunement to both chance and the subtle flows of magic in their environment. They range from petite to tall, standing between three and six feet, with wiry or lithe builds suited to quick movement, climbing, and graceful gestures. Their skin carries a natural, faint glow that can take the form of star-like freckles, soft sigils, or flowing patterns that shift with emotion, magical activity, or sunlight.

Hair ranges from honey and chestnut to copper, gold, and jade tones, often styled in flowing waves, curls, or dramatic braids, adorned with charms, beads, or small enchanted trinkets that reflect personal flair and magical presence. Eyes are expressive and varied, including amber, hazel, deep brown, gold, green, or soft blue, capable of subtle luminescence when Gandiroshas focus their magical or intuitive senses. Their clothing blends practicality with artistry, often layered, flowing, or accented with pouches, charms, and symbols, allowing both freedom of movement and the display of individual style. Gandiroshas possess an innate connection to luck, opportunity, and the hidden currents of events around them, allowing them to sense favorable outcomes, detect subtle threats, and influence social or magical situations through intuition, charm, and clever timing.

They move with remarkable lightness and agility, slipping past obstacles, navigating crowded spaces, or disappearing briefly from sight with fleeting illusions or environmental blending. Their social skills are heightened, drawing vitality and focus from interaction, shared meals, stories, music, or companionship, while isolation, stress, or chaotic surroundings can diminish their magical acuity. Gandiroshas have finely tuned perception, enabling them to read intentions, uncover hidden treasures, detect traps, and anticipate outcomes with uncanny accuracy. Their subtle magic can influence luck, create brief illusions, manipulate small objects, or enhance group morale through presence and charisma.

The combination of agility, charm, and magical sensitivity makes them adept travelers, negotiators, storytellers, and guides, able to thrive in bustling cities, hidden enclaves, or wild landscapes. Emotion, comfort, and aesthetic balance are central to their wellbeing, with personal grooming, clothing, and presentation directly affecting confidence, magical resonance, and social influence. They favor rich, exotic foods, warm communal meals, or foraged delicacies that reinforce vitality and a sense of joy. Gandiroshas are playful, daring, and socially perceptive, turning ordinary interactions into opportunities for influence, amusement, or subtle guidance.

Despite their often whimsical or mischievous demeanor, they are capable, resilient, and remarkably resourceful, able to endure environmental hazards, magical challenges, or social intrigue with creativity and poise. They combine keen intellect with instinctive reaction, making them masters of observation, timing, and subtle manipulation of both people and surroundings. Every aspect of their lives, from movement to clothing, food, and speech, reflects the seamless integration of intuition, magic, and charisma that defines their species.

Every aspect of their lives, from movement to clothing, food, and speech, reflects the seamless integration of intuition, magic, and charisma that defines their species.

sections.heading: Gandirosha Traits
content: Your Gandirosha character has the following racial traits.
Ability Score Increase. Your Dexterity score increases by 2, and your Charisma, Wisdom, or Intelligence score increases by 1.
Creature Type. You are a Humanoid.
Size. You are Small or Medium, chosen when selecting this race.
Speed. Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

Fortune Sense. You gain proficiency in Insight, Perception, Sleight of Hand, or Persuasion. You also have advantage on ability checks made to notice traps, hidden valuables, loaded dice, false smiles, or subtle shifts in social mood.

Lucky Timing. When you fail an ability check, attack roll, or saving throw, you may roll 1d4 and add it to the result, potentially turning failure into success. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and regain all expended uses after a long rest.

Fleeting Glamour. You know minor illusion. Starting at 3rd level, you may cast disguise self once per long rest. Starting at 5th level, you may cast invisibility once per long rest, targeting only yourself. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

Lightfoot Agility. You can move through the space of a creature that is at least one size larger than you. You also ignore nonmagical difficult terrain caused by crowds, clutter, loose rubble, market stalls, furniture, or narrow urban spaces.

Communal Spark. During a short rest, if you share food, music, storytelling, games, or friendly conversation with at least one ally, you and one creature who joined you gain temporary hit points equal to your proficiency bonus.
Languages. You can speak, read, and write Common and one additional language of your choice.

sections.heading: Classes I Point Players Toward
content: Bard, Rogue, Ranger, Monk, Warlock, Sorcerer, or any face/scout role.

sections.heading: Roleplaying Notes
content: Let the character's body language reflect their core concept: agile, socially radiant beings who read opportunity, sense hidden outcomes, and shape fortune through charm and clever timing.
Tie daily needs, grooming, clothing, ritual practice, and social habits to the race's biology instead of treating traits as only combat powers.
I use the race's homeland, bloodline, environmental preference, and magical sustenance as hooks for settlement placement, NPC schedules, family traditions, and adventuring goals.
When a mechanical trait overlaps with a class feature, me as MOL should allow the player to choose the most flavorful option without stacking beyond the table's balance comfort.

sections.heading: MOL Notes for Universal Integration
content: This race is designed to plug into Universal settlements, NPC generators, regional biome logic, and ancestry-aware character creation. When assigning NPCs, prioritize habitats and cultures that match their physical needs and magical affinities.

sections.heading: Universal Alignment Profile
content: Typical race profile: Chaotic Mediator — The unconventional diplomat: socially gifted, improvisational, rule-bending, and usually trying to defuse or redirect conflict.
Gandirosha are luck-touched wanderers built around charm, timing, intuition, and subtle magic. Their strongest alignment pressure is cooperative social improvisation, not obedience to systems.

MOL use: Use Gandirosha as wandering charmers, chance-guides, lucky brokers, messengers, festival magicians, and social fixers. Trickster factions can slide toward Chaotic Knave; heroic guides can rise toward Chaotic Guardian.

player_lore: The Aburatas are a race of infernal beings . They possess two distinct forms that reflect their dual nature: a humanoid form and a quadrupedal, equine-inspired form. In humanoid form, Aburatas have polished, taut skin resembling obsidian, molten iron, or amethyst-violet, often etched with glowing sigils or ember-like vein patterns that pulse with their emotions. Their eyes blaze with infernal fire or sink into abyssal voids, and their hair can range from jet black to flame-red, silver-violet, or stark white.

Horns emerge in unique shapes such as spiraled, antlered, or blade-like, glowing faintly with infernal energy, while a prehensile tail flickers with embers or faint hellfire, aiding balance and expressive gestures. In quadrupedal form, their humanoid upper bodies transition into powerful horse-like torsos sheathed in scaled textures reminiscent of volcanic stone or blackened steel, with muscular limbs ending in broad hooves that leave glowing, smoldering prints. The tail grows longer and more expressive, capable of grasping objects or assisting in movements, while the air around them carries heat and shadow, enhancing their imposing presence. Their voices are resonant and hypnotic, capable of commanding attention or inspiring unease.

Aburatas are sustained by infernal energy rather than ordinary nourishment, drawing vitality from places of power, fire-lit areas, or sites infused with dark influence. They maintain stamina, focus, and resilience through sheer will and magical energy, and their infernal heritage grants them natural resistance to fire, curses, and corruption. Aburatas are highly charismatic, their presence amplifying social influence, persuasion, and intimidation. They exhibit keen dexterity and precision in both combat and manipulation of objects, aided by sharp, clawed hands in humanoid form.

Their movements are fluid, blending grace with the raw strength of their infernal heritage, whether in the upright or quadrupedal form. They thrive in both isolation and positions of influence, drawing strength from ambition, social interaction, or conquest. Aburatas are capable of channeling infernal power through their physical presence, gestures, and even the environment around them, creating an aura of intimidation or allure. They are highly adaptable, capable of thriving in diverse environments, and their appearance—horns, tails, glowing veins, and eyes—conveys both danger and authority.

Their forms, both humanoid and quadrupedal, are a direct reflection of their infernal lineage, with shared traits ensuring identity remains recognizable across transformations. Aburatas require minimal conventional hygiene, maintaining their essence through magical or ritual purification. They are self-reliant and ambitious, with culture and behavior focused on shaping their own destinies and commanding respect or fear. Their dual forms allow them to navigate varied terrains, engage with others socially, and manipulate their surroundings with both physical and magical abilities.

Infernal energy sustains their vitality and focus, and they can maintain activity for extended periods without conventional rest. Aburatas carry the legacy of their infernal ancestry in every aspect of their form, movement, and presence, combining elegance, menace, and supernatural power.

Aburata Traits

Creature Type. You are a Humanoid. You also count as a Fiend for prerequisites, spells, magical effects, or items that specifically affect fiendish creatures.
Size. You are Medium in humanoid form. In quadrupedal form, your body is still treated as Medium for normal play unless me as MOL rules a scene requires special handling.
Speed. Your base walking speed is 30 feet in humanoid form and 40 feet in quadrupedal form.

Dual Infernal Form. As a bonus action, you may shift between humanoid form and quadrupedal equine-inspired form. Your worn equipment merges, resizes, or remains worn as appropriate. In quadrupedal form, you cannot use equipment requiring two humanoid legs, but you gain advantage on ability checks made to run, carry, shove, resist being knocked prone, or traverse rough terrain.
Hellforged Resistance. You have resistance to fire damage. You have advantage on saving throws against curses, magical corruption, and effects that would frighten you.

Infernal Presence. You gain proficiency in Intimidation, Persuasion, Deception, or Performance. When you make a Charisma check against a creature that can see your horns, glowing sigils, ember-veins, or hellfire aura, you may add 1d4 to the roll. player_lore: Deorbasuns are majestic. Their physiques range from muscular, feline-like frames to lithe, agile forms with fur, scales, or earth-toned skin, reflecting a deep connection to predatory grace, wilderness instinct, and mystical energy. Heights vary widely, from six to nine feet, and their limbs are long and flexible, ending in retractable claws or talons capable of channeling energy or venom. Eyes glow with intelligence and authority, displaying hues from ember and gold to crystalline blues, greens, or silver, and often carry faint luminescence that responds to magic or emotion.

Hair and manes vary from obsidian black, smoldering crimson, and radiant gold to bioluminescent strands, shimmered locks, or ethereal highlights, often adorned with beads, feathers, bones, or gemstones marking achievements, lineage, or ritual significance. Wings, tails, or subtle soul-animal traits enhance both presence and ability, with wings capable of flight or generating gusts, tails delivering venom, radiant energy, or prehensile utility, and faint ethereal markings or patterns tying form to instinct and magic. Deorbasuns possess extraordinary physical and magical abilities that blend predatory skill, shapeshifting versatility, and environmental attunement. They can leap with precision, maneuver through air or terrain with grace, and strike with claws, fangs, or tails imbued with energy or venom.

Some can shift subtly to reflect traits of a soul-animal, such as enhanced senses, agility, or elemental affinities, while others maintain a consistently imposing, feline-like or beastly form. Their endurance and stamina are exceptional, allowing them to traverse rugged terrain, hunt, or perform ritualized movement for extended periods. They absorb energy through magical currents, prey, or ambient mana, and their focus and vitality are renewed through hunting, meditation, ritual exposure, or communion with natural and mystical environments. Deorbasuns are highly perceptive, capable of reading subtle environmental cues, sensing magical disturbances, and coordinating with wildlife or allies in ways that reflect both strategic intelligence and instinctual response.

Culturally, Deorbasuns combine reverence for the natural world, mastery of their physical and magical abilities, and a deep sense of honor and hierarchy. They adorn themselves with ritual markings, scars, piercings, or natural ornaments that signify skill, achievement, or spiritual connection. Hunting, dueling, or ritualized stalking is both a means of sustenance and a practice that reinforces mental clarity, magical resonance, and communal status. They maintain hygiene and ceremonial grooming, often utilizing natural waters, smoke cleansing, or volcanic springs, integrating these practices with meditation or reflection under celestial light.

Deorbasuns are guardians of territory, mystical sites, or sacred knowledge, and their presence exerts authority, influence, and subtle intimidation. Their combined attributes of physical prowess, magical attunement, and instinctive intelligence make them versatile, resilient, and commanding beings, fully integrated into the landscapes and mystical currents of Universal.

races.classification: I place this race in Miscellaneous and Hard-to-Classify because it crosses more than one race-family pattern.
races.summary: Ability Score Increase. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.

base_traits.name: Overview
base_traits.description: Your Jaspey character has the following racial traits.

base_traits.name: Ability Score Increase
base_traits.description: Your Dexterity score increases by 2, and your Wisdom or Intelligence score increases by 1.

base_traits.name: Age
base_traits.description: Jaspeys mature rapidly, reaching adulthood around 4 years old. Most live between 25 and 40 years, though ancient fungal sages and colony elders sometimes survive for over a century under ideal conditions.

base_traits.name: Alignment Guidance
base_traits.description: Jaspeys tend toward chaotic or neutral alignments. They value adaptability, freedom, comfort, curiosity, and survival more than laws or rigid traditions. Most Jaspeys are not malicious, though some become selfish scavengers, manipulative tricksters, grave robbers, or unsettling fungal occultists.

base_traits.name: Creature Type
base_traits.description: You are a Humanoid. You are also considered a Plant for any prerequisite, spell, magical effect, or item that specifically affects plant creatures.

base_traits.name: Size
base_traits.description: You are Tiny. Jaspeys are typically between 4 and 8 inches tall and weigh between 1 and 3 pounds. Most can comfortably curl up inside pouches, satchels, coat hoods, helmets, teacups, drawers, backpacks, or small containers. Because of your Tiny size: You can move through the space of any creature Medium or larger. You can occupy the same space as a willing creature Medium or larger. You cannot effectively wield Heavy weapons. I may rule that some weapons, armor, mounts, or equipment must be specially crafted for you.

base_traits.name: Speed
base_traits.description: Your base walking speed is 20 feet. You also have a climbing speed equal to your walking speed.

base_traits.name: Tiny Clinger
base_traits.description: You are exceptionally skilled at climbing onto larger creatures and riding unnoticed. You can occupy the space of a willing creature that is Medium or larger, clinging to their clothing, armor, backpack, shoulder, hood, belt, or hat. While occupying their space: You move with them automatically unless you choose to leave their space. You have half cover against attacks originating outside that creature’s space. You may dismount by spending 5 feet of movement.

base_traits.name: Darkvision
base_traits.description: Accustomed to moonlit forests, tunnels, graveyards, ruins, and dim interiors, you can see in dim light within 60 feet as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You cannot discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

base_traits.name: Spore Puff
base_traits.description: When threatened, Jaspeys instinctively release clouds of irritating fungal spores. As a reaction when a creature within 5 feet of you hits you with a melee attack, you may force that creature to make a Constitution saving throw. The saving throw DC equals: 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier On a failed save, choose one of the following effects: The creature is poisoned until the end of its next turn. The creature cannot take reactions until the end of its next turn. The creature has disadvantage on opportunity attacks until the end of its next turn. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

base_traits.name: Medicinal Harvest
base_traits.description: Your fungal body naturally produces strange medicinal growths. During a long rest, you may harvest spores, mushrooms, molds, oils, or fungal growths from your body to create one fungal remedy. Choose one of the following options:

base_traits.name: Healing Tea
base_traits.description: A creature can drink this tea as an action to regain hit points equal to 1d6 + your proficiency bonus.

base_traits.name: Clarity Spores
base_traits.description: A creature can inhale these spores to gain advantage on the next saving throw it makes against being frightened, poisoned, or diseased within the next hour.

base_traits.name: Drowsy Dust
base_traits.description: As an action, a creature may throw this dust at a target within 10 feet. The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your racial save DC or have its speed reduced to 0 until the start of your next turn. Unused remedies lose potency after 24 hours.

base_traits.name: Scavenger’s Instinct
base_traits.description: You gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: Arcana Medicine Sleight of Hand Stealth You also gain proficiency with one of the following tools: Alchemist’s supplies Herbalism kit Thieves’ tools

base_traits.name: Shiny Obsession
base_traits.description: Jaspeys are instinctively drawn toward reflective, metallic, hidden, and valuable objects. You have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks made to locate or notice: Hidden valuables Coins Jewelry Keys Small metallic objects Reflective surfaces Concealed compartments Additionally, squeezing through spaces large enough for a Tiny creature costs you no extra movement.

base_traits.name: Fungal Resilience
base_traits.description: Your strange biology grants resistance against toxins and rot. You have: Advantage on saving throws against poison and disease Resistance to poison damage

base_traits.name: Pocket Sleeper
base_traits.description: You can complete a long rest while occupying the space of a willing Medium or larger creature, provided you remain undisturbed and have suitable warmth or shelter. Many Jaspeys sleep curled inside hats, cloaks, backpacks, bedrolls, oversized sleeves, or pockets.

base_traits.name: Languages
base_traits.description: You can speak, read, and write: Common Sylvan One additional language of your choice Jaspey speech is often filled with squeaks, raspy chittering, tiny growls, clicks, whispers, and soft fungal humming noises.

subtypes.name: Mosscap
subtypes.canonical_description: Mosscap is a canonical non-bloodline Jaspey form. It does not create a separate ancestry or bloodline.
source_overview: Mosscaps are gentle healers and wandering herbalists covered in soft moss, pale mushrooms, glowing spores, and fragrant medicinal fungi.
They commonly travel with adventurers as medics, alchemists, shamans, or plague doctors.

traits.name: Overview
traits.description: Mosscaps are gentle healers and wandering herbalists covered in soft moss, pale mushrooms, glowing spores, and fragrant medicinal fungi. They commonly travel with adventurers as medics, alchemists, shamans, or plague doctors.

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Wisdom score increases by 1.

traits.name: Soothing Spores
traits.description: As an action, you release calming restorative spores. One creature within 10 feet regains hit points equal to your proficiency bonus. Once you use this trait, you cannot use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

traits.name: Herbal Adept

blocks.text: Jaspey
A player-facing race guide I use as MOL for Universal.

Created by: Nephthysra. I present this race as created by Nephthysra only. Other powers can appear as patrons, rivals, temples, bargains, or local traditions, but they are not creator gods for this race.
My table category: Miscellaneous and Hard-to-Classify Races.
My table classification: I place this race in Miscellaneous and Hard-to-Classify because it crosses more than one race-family pattern.

Tiny fungal raccoon-folk born from ancient symbiotic spores and scavenger spirits, Jaspeys are eerie yet lovable creatures that blur the line between woodland fae, living fungus, and grave-born scavenger. Though their appearance often resembles tiny undead raccoons stitched together with moss, mushrooms, and decay, Jaspeys are fully living beings with beating hearts, warm emotions, and vibrant cultures.

Standing only a few inches tall, Jaspeys can sleep inside coat pockets, teacups, backpacks, hollow books, hat brims, or even small tins. Entire hidden settlements may exist unnoticed inside old walls, cemetery gardens, forgotten cupboards, abandoned wagons, or the roots of ancient trees.

Jaspeys are natural scavengers, herbalists, healers, thieves, potion brewers, and strange little mystics. They collect shiny objects obsessively, form strong emotional bonds with larger companions, and often travel alongside adventuring parties as medics, alchemists, scouts, or magical nuisances.
Despite their unsettling appearance, many Jaspeys are affectionate and deeply social creatures who value comfort, curiosity, survival, and companionship above all else.
Jaspey Traits
Your Jaspey character has the following racial traits.
Ability Score Increase
Your Dexterity score increases by 2, and your Wisdom or Intelligence score increases by 1.
Age

Jaspeys mature rapidly, reaching adulthood around 4 years old. Most live between 25 and 40 years, though ancient fungal sages and colony elders sometimes survive for over a century under ideal conditions.
Alignment Guidance
Jaspeys tend toward chaotic or neutral alignments. They value adaptability, freedom, comfort, curiosity, and survival more than laws or rigid traditions.
Most Jaspeys are not malicious, though some become selfish scavengers, manipulative tricksters, grave robbers, or unsettling fungal occultists.
Creature Type
You are a Humanoid.
You are also considered a Plant for any prerequisite, spell, magical effect, or item that specifically affects plant creatures.
Size
You are Tiny.

Jaspeys are typically between 4 and 8 inches tall and weigh between 1 and 3 pounds. Most can comfortably curl up inside pouches, satchels, coat hoods, helmets, teacups, drawers, backpacks, or small containers.
Because of your Tiny size:
You can move through the space of any creature Medium or larger.
You can occupy the same space as a willing creature Medium or larger.
You cannot effectively wield Heavy weapons.
I may rule that some weapons, armor, mounts, or equipment must be specially crafted for you.
Speed
Your base walking speed is 20 feet.
You also have a climbing speed equal to your walking speed.
Tiny Clinger
You are exceptionally skilled at climbing onto larger creatures and riding unnoticed.
You can occupy the space of a willing creature that is Medium or larger, clinging to their clothing, armor, backpack, shoulder, hood, belt, or hat.
While occupying their space:
You move with them automatically unless you choose to leave their space.
You have half cover against attacks originating outside that creature’s space.
You may dismount by spending 5 feet of movement.
Darkvision
Accustomed to moonlit forests, tunnels, graveyards, ruins, and dim interiors, you can see in dim light within 60 feet as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light.
You cannot discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.
Spore Puff
When threatened, Jaspeys instinctively release clouds of irritating fungal spores.
As a reaction when a creature within 5 feet of you hits you with a melee attack, you may force that creature to make a Constitution saving throw.
The saving throw DC equals:
8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier
On a failed save, choose one of the following effects:
The creature is poisoned until the end of its next turn.
The creature cannot take reactions until the end of its next turn.
The creature has disadvantage on opportunity attacks until the end of its next turn.
You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Medicinal Harvest
Your fungal body naturally produces strange medicinal growths.
During a long rest, you may harvest spores, mushrooms, molds, oils, or fungal growths from your body to create one fungal remedy. Choose one of the following options:
Healing Tea
A creature can drink this tea as an action to regain hit points equal to 1d6 + your proficiency bonus.
Clarity Spores
A creature can inhale these spores to gain advantage on the next saving throw it makes against being frightened, poisoned, or diseased within the next hour.
Drowsy Dust
As an action, a creature may throw this dust at a target within 10 feet.
The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your racial save DC or have its speed reduced to 0 until the start of your next turn.
Unused remedies lose potency after 24 hours.
Scavenger’s Instinct
You gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice:
Arcana
Medicine
Sleight of Hand
Stealth
You also gain proficiency with one of the following tools:
Alchemist’s supplies
Herbalism kit
Thieves’ tools
Shiny Obsession
Jaspeys are instinctively drawn toward reflective, metallic, hidden, and valuable objects.
You have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks made to locate or notice:
Hidden valuables
Coins
Jewelry
Keys
Small metallic objects
Reflective surfaces
Concealed compartments
Additionally, squeezing through spaces large enough for a Tiny creature costs you no extra movement.
Fungal Resilience
Your strange biology grants resistance against toxins and rot.
You have:
Advantage on saving throws against poison and disease
Resistance to poison damage
Pocket Sleeper
You can complete a long rest while occupying the space of a willing Medium or larger creature, provided you remain undisturbed and have suitable warmth or shelter.
Many Jaspeys sleep curled inside hats, cloaks, backpacks, bedrolls, oversized sleeves, or pockets.
Languages
You can speak, read, and write:
Common
Sylvan
One additional language of your choice
Jaspey speech is often filled with squeaks, raspy chittering, tiny growls, clicks, whispers, and soft fungal humming noises.
Jaspey Culture
Jaspey communities are called colonies, though they function more like extended scavenger families than rigid societies.
A single colony may inhabit:
Hollow trees
Graveyards
Sewer tunnels
Old libraries
Traveling wagons
Cemetery walls
Abandoned homes
Giant mushroom groves
The walls of taverns or castles
Most colonies build tiny hidden homes from scavenged debris such as:
Buttons
Moss
Wax
Coins
Bottlecaps
Cloth scraps
Twine
Feathers
Bones
Jewelry fragments
Jaspeys often trade in medicines, alchemical ingredients, scavenged treasures, secret knowledge, and strange favors.
Larger folk frequently mistake them for pests, undead vermin, cursed familiars, or harmless spirits.

Jaspey names are usually short, squeaky, or based on sounds, objects, fungi, weather, or scavenged trinkets.
Male Names
Bram, Nib, Titch, Cork, Sedge, Mott, Wick, Crim, Pock, Velm
Female Names
Mira, Spindle, Tansy, Vella, Pippa, Nettle, Sori, Luma, Wisp, Bristle
Colony Names
The Lantern Mold, Mosshollow, Tinburrow, Rotshade Colony, The Velvet Spores, Candlecap Nest

Different fungal colonies developed unique traits and traditions over centuries of survival.

Additionally, creatures have disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks made to notice you while you occupy another creature’s space.
Rotcap Jaspey
Rotcaps are eerie fungal mystics fascinated by spirits, decay, curses, death magic, and forgotten knowledge.
Their mushrooms are often crimson, purple, black, or sickly white, and many possess glowing eyes or visible skeletal patches beneath their fur.

Additionally, creatures have disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks made to notice you while you occupy another creature’s space.

sections.heading: Rotcap Jaspey
content: Rotcaps are eerie fungal mystics fascinated by spirits, decay, curses, death magic, and forgotten knowledge.
Their mushrooms are often crimson, purple, black, or sickly white, and many possess glowing eyes or visible skeletal patches beneath their fur.
Your Intelligence score increases by 1.
You know the druidcraft cantrip.
Starting at 3rd level, you can cast ray of sickness once with this trait.
Starting at 5th level, you can cast blindness/deafness once with this trait.
You regain the ability to cast these spells when you finish a long rest.
Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for these spells.
You gain proficiency in either:
Arcana
Religion
When making checks related to undead, curses, decay, fungi, spirits, or necromancy, you may add a 1d4 bonus to the roll once per short or long rest.

sections.heading: Universal Alignment Profile
content: Typical race profile: Chaotic Guardian — A wild protector with a golden heart: anti-authoritarian, strange, and deeply protective.
Jaspeys are tiny fungal raccoon-folk: scavenger-spirited, eerie, lovable, communal, and tied to decay/rebirth. Their kindness is real, but their methods are strange, feral, and anti-bureaucratic.
MOL use: Use Jaspeys as grave-garden helpers, mushroom den guardians, fae scavengers, tiny rescue crews, and weirdly brave household spirits. Vengeful rot-clans can become Chaotic Vigilantes.

player_lore: Volsariis are ethereal, multi-limbed beings . They possess four arms as a standard trait, elongated ears that curve upward and nearly resemble horns, and long, sensitive antennae atop their heads that detect changes in the environment, subtle emotions, and spiritual currents. Their skin ranges widely from iridescent shades of deep blues, greens, and storm-gray to luminous pastels, dawn-pinks, or shadowed violets, often streaked or veined with faint magical light, and may carry subtle markings that glow or shift with emotion, spiritual energy, or ambient magic. Their eyes vary from softly glowing gold, silver, and sky-blue to hollow voids, nebula-like patterns, or luminous starlight, reflecting both perception of the physical world and awareness of spirits, dream energy, or hidden currents.

Hair flows lightly or appears almost weightless, with colors spanning metallic, pastel, starlit, or shadowed hues, sometimes giving the impression of liquid light, drifting mist, or feather-like strands. They maintain an elegant, deliberate grace in movement, capable of silent terrestrial motion, climbing, gliding, or, in their final life cycle, sprouting vast wings ranging from feathered to gossamer or ethereal forms, allowing them flight and aerial control that expresses both power and precision. Volsariis act as ferriers of the dead for Nyxarion, guiding souls through liminal spaces and maintaining the balance between life and death. They are attuned to both the waking and spiritual realms, able to sense, communicate with, and influence spirits, manage transitions, and preserve memory through subtle manipulation of energy, aura, or pheromones.

Their abilities blend ethereal perception, dream- or shadow-influenced magic, and radiant or elemental powers, allowing them to phase through matter, weave illusions, manipulate light, wind, or celestial energies, and project calming, inspiring, or disorienting auras. Rituals, meditation, and communion with sacred or magical sites restore vitality, while harsh, chaotic, or energy-depleted environments can diminish focus and magical resonance. Volsariis draw sustenance primarily from ambient magic, spiritual energy, or dream currents rather than conventional food, though symbolic consumption may accompany ceremonial practices. Their culture emphasizes cycles, reflection, guardianship, guidance, and balance, blending artistic expression, dreamwork, and ritual observances with precise attention to the flow of life, death, and magical currents.

Physically and magically, Volsariis exhibit remarkable versatility and resilience. Their four arms allow multitasking, combat, or ceremonial dexterity, while their antennae and long ears enhance awareness, environmental perception, and subtle communication. They can project light, shadow, or elemental energy, manipulate perception and memory, phase between corporeal and ethereal forms, and in advanced stages manifest wings for flight. Their presence is simultaneously serene and commanding, blending subtle authority, spiritual guidance, and ethereal beauty.

They can influence emotion, perception, and even dream or spiritual experiences through gestures, voice, or aura. Volsariis thrive as guardians, guides, and mediators of souls, capable of balancing powerful abilities with patient observation, ritualized practice, and attunement to both natural and supernatural forces in Universal.

Their skin ranges widely from iridescent shades of deep blues, greens, and storm-gray to luminous pastels, dawn-pinks, or shadowed violets, often streaked or veined with faint magical light, and may carry subtle markings that glow or shift with emotion, spiritual energy, or ambient magic. Volsariis draw sustenance primarily from ambient magic, spiritual energy, or dream currents rather than conventional food, though symbolic consumption may accompany ceremonial practices. Physically and magically, Volsariis exhibit remarkable versatility and resilience. They can project light, shadow, or elemental energy, manipulate perception and memory, phase between corporeal and ethereal forms, and in advanced stages manifest wings for flight. Volsarii Traits
Your Volsarii character has the following racial traits.
Ability Score Increase. Increase your Wisdom or Charisma score by 2, and increase one other ability score by 1.

Creature Type. You are a Humanoid. You also count as a Celestial or Fey for prerequisites, spells, magical effects, or items that specifically affect liminal, spirit-touched, or otherworldly beings, chosen when selecting this race.
Size. You are Medium.
Speed. Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

Four Arms. You have four arms. The secondary pair can hold objects, perform somatic components, open doors, carry tools, or interact with items. They do not grant extra attacks, additional shields, or extra two-handed weapon use unless me as MOL allows a specific feature to do so.

Antennae and Spirit Senses. You gain proficiency in Insight, Perception, or Religion. You have advantage on checks made to notice emotional shifts, spiritual residue, undead presence, or changes in magical atmosphere.

Ferrier of the Dead. You know spare the dying. At 3rd level, you may cast protection from evil and good once per long rest. At 5th level, you may cast gentle repose or augury once per long rest. Wisdom or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

Liminal Step. As a bonus action, you may become partially ethereal until the end of your turn. During this movement, you may move through the space of creatures and ignore nonmagical difficult terrain. If you end your turn inside an object, you are shunted to the nearest open space and take force damage equal to your level. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

Winged Final Cycle. Your wings begin as spiritual, feathered, gossamer, or ethereal structures. When you fall, you may use your reaction to glide and reduce falling damage by five times your level. At 5th level, you may fly for 1 minute at a speed of 30 feet once per long rest.
Languages. You can speak, read, and write Common and one language associated with spirits, celestial courts, shadow realms, or ancestral rites.

races.name: Gwynis
races.summary: Dream-Born Ethereals of Illusion, Memory, and Psychic Insight. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.
player_lore: Gwynises are ethereal, dream-born beings . Their appearances range widely, from tall, slender, shadow-touched figures to luminous, starlit forms with flowing, weightless hair and shifting, aurora-like or mist-like skin patterns that reflect thought, emotion, or ambient magical energy. Eyes vary from glowing moons and crystalline orbs to hollow voids or softly luminescent shades, capable of perceiving layers of reality, psychic echoes, or dreamscapes. Their bodies can phase between tangible and ghostly states, trailing wisps, shadowed tendrils, or dreamlike distortions that ripple with their movements, and their fingers and limbs are long, dexterous, and capable of absorbing mana, manipulating subtle forces, or projecting dream energy.

Gwynises move with fluid grace and silent precision, able to influence perception, subtly manipulate emotion, or weave ephemeral illusions and constructs from thought, dream, and psychic resonance. They thrive in magical, artistic, or low-light environments, sustaining themselves through dream energy, meditation, ambient magic, or symbolic nourishment, while chaotic or harsh surroundings can diminish focus, well-being, and psychic attunement. Gwynises possess a versatile range of abilities that blend ethereal grace, dreamcraft, and subtle guardianship. They can obscure themselves, manipulate perception, cloud memory, or guide and protect others through psychic insight and dream influence.

They are capable of lucid dreamcraft, weaving illusions, threading thought into reality, and sensing hidden truths or intentions in both waking and dream realms. Their physical and metaphysical forms are resilient, enduring environmental extremes while maintaining grace, or phasing through matter and shadows when needed. Some Gwynises manifest ephemeral or surreal adornments, levitating objects, flowing tattoos, or subtle elemental or celestial effects that mirror their inner state. They can influence emotion and perception through presence, pheromones, or vocal resonance, and their aura often bends reality subtly around them, inspiring awe, creativity, or reflection in observers.

Culturally, Gwynises center on art, metaphor, and the weaving of communal and personal narratives into both dream and waking spaces. They practice ceremonies that explore insight, balance, emotion, and foresight, creating dreamwoven sanctuaries, symbolic constructs, and spaces for guidance, ritual, and learning. They maintain harmony through meditation, environmental attunement, and psychic or dream-based exercises, combining emotional expression with precise manipulation of magical and metaphysical currents. Gwynises often act as seers, dream guides, mediators, or subtle influencers, shaping perception without overt force.

They are guardians of dream spaces, memory, and hidden truths, blending imagination, intuition, and ethereal presence to protect, inspire, and guide. Crosses with other magically attuned or mystical beings enhance specific abilities, such as dreamwalking, elemental resonance, or metaphysical insight, producing a diverse spectrum of forms and talents, while incompatible unions may require magical or ritual intervention to succeed. Their society values creativity, empathy, subtlety, and attunement to both magical and psychic energies, producing individuals capable of profound insight, guidance, and influence across Universal.

base_traits.name: Ability Score Increase
base_traits.description: Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score by 2, and increase one other ability score by 1.

base_traits.name: Creature Type
base_traits.description: You are a Humanoid. You also count as a Fey for prerequisites, spells, magical effects, or items that specifically affect fey creatures.

base_traits.name: Size
base_traits.description: You are Small or Medium, chosen when selecting this race.

base_traits.name: Speed
base_traits.description: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

base_traits.name: Dreamsight
base_traits.description: You have darkvision out to 60 feet. While in dim light, darkness, dreams, magical mist, or an illusion, you can tell whether a creature within 30 feet is awake, asleep, frightened, charmed, or under an illusion, unless that creature is protected by magic that blocks divination.

base_traits.name: Lucid Dreamcraft
base_traits.description: You know minor illusion. At 3rd level, you may cast silent image once per long rest. At 5th level, you may cast phantasmal force or calm emotions once per long rest. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells, chosen when selecting this race.

base_traits.name: Ethereal Flicker
base_traits.description: As a reaction when you take damage, you may partially phase. Reduce the damage by an amount equal to your proficiency bonus + the modifier of your chosen spellcasting ability. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

base_traits.name: Memory Threader
base_traits.description: You gain proficiency in Insight, Performance, Persuasion, or Stealth. You have advantage on checks made to interpret symbolism, dreams, artistic metaphors, emotional echoes, or psychic impressions.

base_traits.name: Dream Rest
base_traits.description: You do not sleep in the ordinary way. During a long rest, you enter a lucid meditative dream for 4 hours while remaining dimly aware of your surroundings.

base_traits.name: Languages
base_traits.description: You can speak, read, and write Common and Sylvan or one language tied to dream, spirit, or arcane traditions.
